investors.name: Sequoia (India) / Peak XV
investors.thesis: Full-stack partner backing founders from seed to IPO across India and Southeast Asia; build enduring companies, increasingly AI-focused.
investors.notes: Independent since 2023 Sequoia split. ~$9B AUM across 13 funds; 440+ cos, 39 unicorns, 26+ IPOs (Zomato, Meesho, Groww, Wakefit). Raised ~$1.3B in 2026. Runs Surge (170+ startups). Led by Shailendra Singh.
investors.writeup: Peak XV Partners is the leading venture and growth firm across India and Southeast Asia, operating independently since its 2023 separation from Sequoia Capital. It manages roughly $9 billion across 13 funds and has backed over 440 companies in 19 years, producing 39 unicorns and more than two dozen public listings, including Zomato, Meesho, Groww and Wakefit. In early 2026 it raised about $1.3 billion across three vehicles — an India seed fund, an India venture fund and an APAC fund — with most capital earmarked for India. Peak XV runs a full-stack model spanning seed to pre-IPO. Its Surge program (launched 2019) gives early-stage founders up to $3 million in seed capital plus company-building workshops and a global operator community; over 170 startups and 400+ founders have gone through it. Series A cheques typically range $8–16 million, with deep follow-on reserves for winners. The team of ~89, including 16 partners across Bengaluru and Singapore, is led by Shailendra Singh and is increasingly focused on AI and cross-border opportunities. With one of Asia's largest portfolios and an integrated seed-to-IPO platform, Peak XV remains the default institutional partner for the region's most ambitious technology founders.

investors.name: Kalaari Capital
investors.thesis: Back the unknown Indian entrepreneur poised to become tomorrow's global leader; partner early with technology and tech-enabled founders and lead rounds, nurturing them across the growth journey.
investors.notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2006 as Indo-US Venture Partners (NEA partnership); rebranded Kalaari 2012. Founders Vani Kola & Vinod Dham. ~$650M AUM, 157 cos, 8 unicorns, 3 IPOs, 31 acquisitions. Portfolio: Myntra, Cult.fit, BlueStone, Digantara. Team 29 incl 11 partners.
investors.writeup: Kalaari Capital is one of India's pioneering early-stage technology venture firms, founded in 2006 by Vani Kola and Vinod Dham as Indo-US Venture Partners — a partnership with NEA — and rebranded as Kalaari in 2012. Headquartered in Bengaluru, it manages approximately $650 million across its funds and is led by Managing Director Vani Kola, who spent 22 years building and exiting technology companies in Silicon Valley before returning to India. That operator-turned-investor perspective shapes Kalaari's founder-first, mentorship-led approach. The firm invests primarily at seed and Series A, writing cheques of roughly $500K to $5 million, and prefers to lead rounds while reserving capital for follow-on participation; average seed rounds run about $2.2 million and Series A near $4.85 million. Across 19 years it has backed around 157 companies, producing 8 unicorns, 3 IPOs and 31 acquisitions, with notable names including Myntra, Cult.fit, BlueStone and, more recently, space-data startup Digantara. Its team of 29, including 11 partners, spans technology, consumer, fintech and operations expertise. Beyond capital, Kalaari operates as a thought-leadership and community engine, offering portfolio companies structured playbooks and domain knowledge. The firm is also a champion of first-time and diverse founders, reflecting Kola's philosophy of recognising and scaling ambitious early entrepreneurs.

investors.name: Nexus Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Back extraordinary founders building product-first companies that redefine categories across the world's two largest startup ecosystems — the US and India; be the first institutional investor and partner from day one.
investors.notes: Founded 2006. HQ Menlo Park + Bengaluru/Mumbai. ~$3.2B AUM across 11 funds; Fund VIII $700M (Dec 2025, largest global VC fund of 2025), Fund VII $700M (2023). 130+ active cos, 16 unicorns, 11 IPOs. Portfolio: Delhivery, Postman, Zepto, Rapido, Infra.Market, Turtlemint. GPs: Suvir Sujan, Anup Gupta (India); Jishnu Bhattacharjee, Abhishek Sharma (US).
investors.writeup: Nexus Venture Partners is a pioneering cross-border venture capital firm built specifically around the two largest startup ecosystems in the world — the United States and India. Founded in 2006, it operates from Menlo Park alongside Bengaluru and Mumbai, and manages roughly $3.2 billion across eleven funds. In December 2025 it closed its eighth fund at $700 million — described as the largest venture fund raised globally that year — deliberately splitting capital between US-based AI investments and India-focused opportunities; its seventh fund (2023) was also $700 million. Nexus typically acts as the first institutional investor at inception, seed and Series A, writing cheques from about $500K to $10 million, taking a board seat, and reserving capital for follow-on rounds. Its focus spans AI, enterprise software and infrastructure, consumer technology, fintech and commerce. Across nearly 20 years it has backed more than 130 active companies, producing 16 unicorns and 11 IPOs, including Delhivery, Postman, Zepto, Rapido, Infra.Market and Turtlemint, and has returned significant liquidity through exits such as Delhivery, PubMatic, MapmyIndia and Unicommerce. The firm — led by general partners Suvir Sujan and Anup Gupta in India and Jishnu Bhattacharjee and Abhishek Sharma in the US — encourages Indian portfolio companies to establish US operations early, bridging talent and capital across both markets.

investors.name: Sanjay Mehta
investors.thesis: First-cheque angel backing disruptive early-stage founders across India and the US; plays the power law — focus on the magnitude of a few outsized successes rather than frequency, holding 3–5 years for outcomes.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Angel since 2011; 150–230+ personal investments. Founder/Partner 100X.VC (SEBI AIF, sponsored by Mehta Ventures family office). 4 unicorns: OYO (280x exit), CoinDCX, Block.One, AXIOM Space. Portfolio: OYO, Wow! Momo, Box8, LogiNext, Unbxd, PrettySecrets, Coolberg, InstaSafe.
investors.writeup: Sanjay Mehta is among the most prolific and successful angel investors in India, a Mumbai-based serial entrepreneur who has been a first-cheque backer of early-stage startups since 2011. Before investing, he founded MAIA Intelligence, later acquired by Datamatics. Across his personal career he has backed somewhere between 150 and 230+ startups in India and the US, and is widely cited as the only Indian angel with four unicorns to his name: OYO, crypto exchange CoinDCX, blockchain company Block.One, and US space-infrastructure firm AXIOM Space. His most celebrated outcome was a roughly 280x return from an early OYO position; a partial exit from Block.One returned several thousand percent in under three years. Mehta articulates a power-law philosophy — that a small fraction of a portfolio drives almost all returns, so investors should optimise for the magnitude of success, not its frequency, and be patient across three-to-five-year horizons. In December 2019 he institutionalised this approach by founding 100X.VC, India's first fund to invest using iSAFE (India SAFE) notes, sponsored by his Mehta Ventures family office, with an ambition to back 100 startups a year. Notable portfolio names include OYO, Wow! Momo, Box8, LogiNext, Unbxd, PrettySecrets, Coolberg and InstaSafe. He is also a prominent blogger and ecosystem thought leader.

investors.name: Kunal Shah
investors.thesis: Founder-angel backing consumer-internet and fintech businesses that leverage trust, data and distribution to reshape Indian markets; brings deep behavioural-economics insight and strong ecosystem signalling.
investors.chequeSize: Individual angel cheques (typically undisclosed; often part of a syndicate/consortium)
investors.notes: Founder of CRED (2018) and FreeCharge (acquired by Snapdeal). One of India's most prolific founder-investors: 260–290+ startups backed, ~11–13 unicorns. Portfolio: Razorpay, Unacademy, Spinny, Slice, BharatPe, Khatabook, Zetwork, Shiprocket, Nothing (Carl Pei). Board: CRED, Happay, Pine Labs; advisor to Y Combinator and Peak XV.
investors.writeup: Kunal Shah is one of India's most influential entrepreneurs and its single most prolific founder-turned-angel investor. He first built FreeCharge, a digital payments and recharge platform later acquired by Snapdeal, before founding CRED in 2018 — a fintech platform rewarding creditworthy users that has grown into one of the country's most prominent unicorns. His personal wealth, largely tied to his CRED stake, is estimated around $500–600 million. As an angel, Shah has backed more than 260 startups across India and the US — the largest such portfolio of any Indian founder-investor — of which roughly a dozen have become unicorns. His investments span Razorpay, Unacademy, Spinny, Slice, BharatPe, Khatabook, Zetwork, Shiprocket and even Carl Pei's consumer-electronics venture Nothing, reflecting a thesis rooted in consumer internet, fintech and trust-and-distribution-driven businesses. Shah is known for sharp, contrarian thinking grounded in behavioural economics, frequently shared with a large public following, and his participation in a round carries strong signalling value in the ecosystem. Beyond writing cheques, he holds board seats at CRED, Happay and Pine Labs and has advised Y Combinator and Peak XV (Sequoia India). His blend of operator credibility, network depth and brand equity makes him a highly sought-after early backer for India's most ambitious consumer and fintech founders.

investors.name: Anand Chandrasekaran
investors.companyTypeRaw: Angel Investor / VC (Managing Partner, Celesta Capital)
investors.thesis: Back product-led founders building across the India–US corridor, drawing on two decades of operating experience at global platforms to help with product, GTM and cross-border scaling.
investors.notes: Ex-CPO/product leader at Five9, Meta (Messenger), Bharti Airtel, Snapdeal/FreeCharge; founder of Aeroprise (acq. BMC). 80+ angel investments, ~10 unicorns; ranked #1 India–US seed investor by Hurun 2022–24. Former Partner at General Catalyst (built India–US practice); now Managing Partner, Celesta Capital; co-founded Crescendo & HiOctave. Portfolio: MoEngage, Rupeek, DealShare, NoBroker, FPL/OneCard, Exotel, Scaler, SAFE Security.
investors.writeup: Anand Chandrasekaran is one of the most recognised angel investors operating across the India–US technology corridor, and a seasoned product executive. Over two decades he served as a product leader at Five9 — where he helped grow revenue from roughly $120M to $600M ARR — Meta's Messenger Platform, Bharti Airtel and Snapdeal/FreeCharge, and earlier founded Aeroprise, acquired by BMC Software. Since 2015 he has made more than 80 angel investments, around ten of which have become unicorns, and was ranked the #1 seed investor focused on the India–US corridor by the Hurun India report for three consecutive years (2022–2024). His portfolio spans enterprise software, AI, fintech and consumer, including MoEngage, Rupeek, DealShare, NoBroker, FPL Technologies (OneCard), Exotel, Scaler and SAFE Security. He brings a distinctive operator's lens to early-stage investing — deep product intuition and a global network — helping founders with product strategy, go-to-market and cross-border expansion. After establishing the India–US investing practice as a Partner at General Catalyst, where he also co-created the AI-first contact-centre company Crescendo, he is now Managing Partner at Celesta Capital, a deep-tech focused firm, while continuing to back founders. A Stanford graduate, he was named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader and to Fortune India's 40-under-40.

investors.name: Kunal Bahl
investors.thesis: Back passionate, driven founders early across consumer tech, fintech, SaaS, consumer brands, healthtech and B2B services; lead seed rounds and double down on winners through later rounds.
investors.notes: Co-founder of Snapdeal & AceVector (also Unicommerce, Stellaro Brands); Shark Tank India S4 judge. Titan Capital (with Rohit Bansal) investing since 2011: 250–280+ startups. Winners Fund = SEBI Cat-II AIF, ₹333 Cr final close (2024), follow-on into ~20 winners. Portfolio: Ola, Urban Company, Razorpay, Mamaearth, OfBusiness, Unicommerce, Credgenics.
investors.writeup: Kunal Bahl is a pioneering Indian technology entrepreneur and one of the country's most active founder-investors. He co-founded Snapdeal in 2010 with Rohit Bansal, building it into one of India's largest e-commerce platforms, and today chairs AceVector, the holding company for Snapdeal, Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands. Alongside Bansal he runs Titan Capital, an early-stage investment firm through which the pair have backed more than 250–280 startups since 2011 — initially entirely from their own capital. Titan Capital is sector-agnostic but emphasises passionate, driven founders across consumer tech, fintech, SaaS, consumer brands, healthtech and B2B services, typically leading seed rounds with cheques of roughly $300K–$500K through its proprietary Titan Seed Fund. Its portfolio includes some of India's biggest successes — Ola, Urban Company, Razorpay, Mamaearth, OfBusiness, Unicommerce and Credgenics. In 2024 the firm raised external capital for the first time via the Titan Capital Winners Fund, a SEBI Category-II AIF that closed at ₹333 crore and is dedicated to follow-on investments in around 20 of its best-performing portfolio companies at an average ticket of about ₹15 crore. A judge on Shark Tank India and a member of the National Startup Advisory Council, Bahl is among the most influential voices in Indian entrepreneurship.

investors.name: Gaurav Munjal
investors.thesis: Back passionate founders with disruptive ideas in early-stage technology, drawing on edtech and consumer-internet operating experience to mentor on product and scaling.
investors.notes: Co-founder & CEO of Unacademy (founded 2015, edtech unicorn, peaked ~$3.4B). Earlier founded Flatchat (acq. CommonFloor 2014); also Graphy, Airlearn. Angel in ~48–63 startups across India & US. Portfolio: Pine Labs, Pratilipi, Ultrahuman, Rheo TV, TapChief, Lissun, Gully Labs.
investors.writeup: Gaurav Munjal is the co-founder and CEO of Unacademy, one of India's largest online learning platforms, and an active early-stage angel investor. He began as a technologist and entrepreneur, founding the student-accommodation app Flatchat (acquired by CommonFloor in 2014) before building Unacademy — which started as a YouTube channel in 2010 and was formally founded in 2015 with Roman Saini, Hemesh Singh and Sumit Jain. Under his leadership Unacademy grew into an edtech unicorn, reaching a peak valuation of roughly $3.4 billion after a 2020 SoftBank-led round, and he has since steered it toward profitability while also launching ventures like Graphy and Airlearn. As an angel, Munjal has backed somewhere between 48 and 63 startups across India and the US, spanning edtech, consumer technology, SaaS, media and entertainment, enterprise software and gaming. His portfolio includes Pine Labs, Pratilipi, Ultrahuman, Rheo TV, TapChief, Lissun and Gully Labs. He typically invests at pre-seed and seed and is known for backing founders with strong conviction and product clarity, offering mentorship on scaling consumer products in emerging markets. As one of India's most prominent edtech founders and a vocal advocate for its startup ecosystem, his backing carries meaningful signalling value for early-stage founders.

investors.name: Ritesh Agarwal
investors.thesis: Make value-add, operationally-oriented investments in companies with proven unit economics, ~20% YoY growth and $1–10M revenue, partnering with high-repute entrepreneurs building long-lasting businesses.
investors.notes: Founder/CEO of OYO. Personal vehicle Aroa Ventures (Singapore, est. 2020), sponsored by RACo Holding, 100% controlled by Agarwal, headed by Gaurav Gulati (ex-Innov8 COO). ~₹418 Cr AUM, ~45 investments. Portfolio: ZipLoan, Fashalot, Atomberg, GIFSKEY, Wysh, Shyle. Also Shark Tank India guest investor.
investors.writeup: Ritesh Agarwal is the founder and CEO of OYO, the SoftBank-backed global hospitality company, and one of India's youngest self-made billionaires. He channels his personal investing through Aroa Ventures, a Singapore-based firm he established in 2020, sponsored by his RACo Holding Company and fully controlled by him, with day-to-day operations led by Gaurav Gulati, the former COO of Innov8 (which OYO acquired in 2019). Aroa focuses on early and growth-stage businesses across consumer, technology and leisure-infrastructure sectors, and is explicitly operationally oriented — seeking companies with proven unit economics, roughly 20% year-on-year growth and $1–10 million in annual revenue, run by high-repute entrepreneurs building long-lasting businesses. The firm writes cheques between $500K and $5 million (about ₹4–41 crore) and, beyond capital, helps portfolio companies accelerate growth and improve risk-adjusted returns. Aroa manages around ₹418 crore and has made roughly 45 investments, with sector exposure spanning software, media and entertainment, finance and retail; named portfolio companies include ZipLoan, Fashalot, Atomberg Technologies, GIFSKEY, Wysh and, via Shark Tank India, Shyle. Agarwal's scaling experience across 80-plus countries gives him a distinctive global operating perspective on unit economics, distribution and expansion that founders value alongside his capital and brand.

investors.name: Anupam Mittal
investors.thesis: Back scalable, innovative solutions to real-life problems across tech and consumer/D2C; an operator-investor who mentors founders on building and scaling, with a sharp eye on unit economics.
investors.chequeSize: Individual angel cheques (Shark Tank S1–S3: ~INR 1.89 Cr across 55+ deals)
investors.notes: Founder/CEO People Group (Shaadi.com, Makaan.com, Mauj Mobile). Angel since 2007 (first: Interactive Avenues). 200–250+ startups; Shark Tank India judge S1–S3. Portfolio: Ola, BigBasket, Rapido, Rupeek, Druva, Agnikul, FarEye, NxtWave, Animall, Whatfix, plus D2C (Skippi, Hair Originals).
investors.writeup: Anupam Mittal is one of India's most recognisable entrepreneurs and prolific angel investors, best known as the founder and CEO of Shaadi.com — among the world's largest matrimonial platforms — and of People Group, which also operates Makaan.com and Mauj Mobile, India's first mobile-gaming and value-added-services company. Born in Mumbai in 1971 and educated at Boston College, he pioneered internet-based consumer services in India from the late 1990s. He began angel investing in 2007 with Interactive Avenues (a digital advertising agency that became his most successful early bet) and has since backed more than 200–250 startups across consumer internet, D2C, fintech, e-commerce, SaaS, deep tech, clean tech and healthcare. His portfolio includes Ola, BigBasket, Rapido, Rupeek, Druva, Agnikul, FarEye, NxtWave, Animall and Whatfix, alongside numerous D2C brands such as Skippi and Hair Originals. Mittal reached a far wider audience as a judge on Shark Tank India across its first three seasons, where he invested roughly ₹1.89 crore across 55-plus businesses and became known for sharp questioning around unit economics, founder credibility and defensibility. His investment philosophy centres on backing scalable, innovative solutions to real problems, and his blend of operator credibility, capital and mass-media visibility makes him a high-signal early backer.

investors.name: Indian Angel Network (IAN)
investors.thesis: India's largest early-stage investment platform: combine a pan-India angel community with SEBI-registered funds to back early-stage tech founders — including first-generation founders in Tier-II/III cities — with capital plus deep mentorship.
investors.notes: Now IAN Group (founded 2006). Funds: IAN Angel Fund (evergreen), IAN Alpha Fund (SEBI Cat-II, $100M/INR 900 Cr final close Dec 2025), BioAngels. 225+ portfolio cos, 3 unicorns; catalysed ~INR 18,000 Cr. Leadership: Padmaja Ruparel (co-founder), Chintan Thakkar (Group CEO, ex-Info Edge), Vinod Keni, Priyank Garg. Portfolio: Druva, Spinny, Uniphore, FarEye, Zypp Electric.
investors.writeup: Indian Angel Network — now IAN Group — is India's largest and one of its oldest early-stage investment platforms, founded in 2006. It pairs a pan-India community of angel investors with a family of SEBI-registered venture funds, giving founders both capital and deep operator mentorship. The platform has built a portfolio of more than 225 companies, including three unicorns, and claims to have catalysed roughly INR 18,000 crore of follow-on investment and helped create tens of thousands of jobs. Its structure spans the evergreen IAN Angel Fund, the BioAngels vertical, and the IAN Alpha Fund — a SEBI Category-II vehicle that marked its final close at $100 million (about INR 900 crore) in December 2025, with a notable share of investments in first-generation founders across Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Collaborative angel cheques average around INR 1.2 crore, with larger amounts deployed through the Alpha Fund and top-ups into existing portfolio companies. IAN invests across AI/ML, deep tech, biotech, fintech, consumer, healthtech, spacetech and the MSME category. Its leadership includes co-founder Padmaja Ruparel and Group CEO Chintan Thakkar (former Info Edge CFO), alongside Vinod Keni and Priyank Garg. Portfolio names include Druva, Spinny, Uniphore, FarEye, Zypp Electric and Manastu Space.

investors.name: Zeropearl VC
investors.thesis: 'Founder-only' approach — be the first significant backer at pre-seed when conviction matters more than metrics; decide in 7 days, wire within 30, then partner seed-to-IPO. Sector-agnostic, leaning Consumer (D2C/B2C) and SaaS/GenAI.
investors.chequeSize: Lead pre-seed/F&F rounds; targets ~8% ownership; ~12–15 startups/yr (~45 from Fund I)
investors.notes: Gurugram. Founded 2024 by solo GP Bipin Shah (IIT Bombay; ex-Partner/MD Titan Capital; 14 yrs early-stage, evaluated ~50,000 startups, met 5,000+ founders, backed 250+). Fund I INR 159 Cr (~$18M), final close Oct 2025, 3.5x oversubscribed; 52% from 31 founder-LPs incl 18 unicorn founders (e.g. Aman Gupta/boAt). Portfolio: Gully Labs, Frex, Supply 6, SteamPRO. Past bets (via Titan): Mamaearth, Credgenics, InVideo, Giva, CityMall; exits Beardo, Oziva, SuprDaily.
investors.writeup: Zeropearl VC is a solo-GP, pre-seed and seed-stage micro-fund founded in 2024 and based in Gurugram, established by Bipin Shah — an IIT Bombay alumnus and former partner/managing director at Titan Capital with over 14 years in early-stage investing. Shah's personal track record is among the most prolific in India: he has evaluated more than 50,000 startups, met thousands of founders, and backed 250-plus ventures, with early bets on Mamaearth, Credgenics, InVideo, Giva and CityMall, and exits including Beardo (acquired by Marico), Oziva (HUL) and SuprDaily (Swiggy). Zeropearl closed its maiden fund at INR 159 crore (about $18 million) in October 2025, oversubscribed more than 3.5 times against an INR 80 crore target before being capped to retain selectivity; notably, 52% of the corpus came from 31 founder-LPs, including 18 unicorn founders such as boAt's Aman Gupta, who provide operational mentorship and network access alongside capital. The fund follows a distinctive 'founder-only' philosophy — aiming to be the first significant backer at the friends-and-family or pre-seed stage — and a rapid, conviction-led process: a yes-or-no answer within seven days and funds wired within 30. It is sector-agnostic with a lean toward consumer (D2C/B2C) and SaaS/GenAI, targets roughly 8% ownership, and plans to back around 45 startups, guiding them toward a strong Series A within 15 months. Portfolio names include Gully Labs, Frex and Supply 6.

investors.name: Premji Invest
investors.thesis: Evergreen, crossover capital backing emerging and disruptive technologies and category-leading companies with enduring value built to thrive in public markets; returns primarily support the Azim Premji Foundation.
investors.notes: Family office of Azim Premji (Wipro), founded 2006, Bengaluru + US. Multi-billion-dollar AUM across private (early/growth/buyout) and public markets. 124+ cos, 27 unicorns. Team ~84 incl 19 partners. Portfolio: Flipkart, Purplle, LambdaTest, GIVA, The Sleep Company, KreditBee, Dezerv. Returns fund Azim Premji Foundation.
investors.writeup: Premji Invest is the investment arm of Azim Premji, founder of Wipro, and one of India's most significant and distinctive capital allocators. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Bengaluru with a US presence, it operates as an evergreen, crossover firm investing across both private and public markets — spanning early-stage (Series A and B), growth equity, buyouts and public equities — with a multi-billion-dollar asset base. Its focus areas are technology, consumer, financial services, healthcare and industrials, and it is known for patient, long-duration capital rather than fixed fund cycles. A defining feature is its purpose: the returns Premji Invest generates primarily fund the Azim Premji Foundation, a non-profit working to improve the lives of India's underserved. The firm has backed more than 120 companies, including 27 unicorns, with named investments such as Flipkart, Purplle, LambdaTest, GIVA, The Sleep Company, KreditBee and Dezerv, and it frequently co-invests with global institutions like BlackRock. Late-stage cheques have historically run in the $20–60 million range, rising to $100 million-plus, while a dedicated early-stage practice partners with Series A/B teams building global companies with public-market ambitions. With a team of around 84 including 19 partners, Premji Invest's backing is widely regarded as a strong signal of company quality and governance.

investors.name: Unicorn India Ventures
investors.thesis: Back early-stage, technology-focused founders building defensible IP with a clear path to profitability; Fund III is ~80% focused on deep-tech, semiconductor, space and defence.
investors.notes: Founded 2015 by Bhaskar Majumdar & Anil Joshi (Mumbai). 3 funds; Fund III ~INR 1,200 Cr. Portfolio 60+ incl. Open (unicorn), Sequretek, Genrobotics, Pharmarack, SmartCoin, EyeROV, OrbitAID.
investors.writeup: Unicorn India Ventures (UIV) is a Mumbai-based, SEBI-registered early-stage venture fund founded in 2015 by Bhaskar Majumdar and Anil Joshi. It invests as the first institutional cheque in technology-focused founders building defensible intellectual property with a clear path to profitability, and is deliberately contrarian — avoiding hype-driven sectors. Across three funds UIV has built an active portfolio of more than 60 companies, including its neobanking unicorn Open, plus Sequretek, Genrobotics, Pharmarack, SmartCoin, EyeROV and OrbitAID, and has seen multiple acquisitions. Its third fund, closing near INR 1,200 crore, marks a sharp pivot toward deep technology: roughly 80% of capital is earmarked for semiconductor design, space and defence, alongside SaaS, fintech, climate-tech and agritech. UIV typically writes initial cheques of around $1–2 million (about INR 10 crore) and reserves substantial follow-on capital — up to $10–15 million — for its strongest companies, deploying only a portion of the corpus initially and concentrating reserves on winners. Fund III's limited partners are split roughly evenly between international investors, domestic institutions, and Indian family offices and UHNIs. The founders bring an unusual blend of media, corporate and angel-network experience, and Anil Joshi is known for candid, governance-focused mentorship of founders.

investors.name: Sun Icon Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest in early-stage disruptive startups 'building the India of tomorrow', combining technology with impact; integrity- and trust-led, long-term partnerships over quick wins. Deliberately avoids me-too consumer brands, generic SaaS and fintech.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2022 by Suresh Jain (ex-Networth; founder Sun Capital/Sun Global; 3+ decades in capital markets) with children Saloni Jain & Darshan Jain as founding partners. Backed by an industrial family-office network. Maiden fund closed. Portfolio: Suind (drones), Dhiway (blockchain), Omnivio, AjnaLens, CultYvate, Vidyakul.
investors.writeup: Sun Icon Ventures is a Mumbai-based early-stage venture capital fund founded in 2022 by capital-markets veteran Suresh Jain, alongside his children Saloni and Darshan Jain as founding partners. Jain spent decades on the sell-side — exiting Networth after the 2008 crisis to build Sun Capital and Sun Global — before transitioning to the buy-side with Sun Icon, backed by a multi-decade industrial family-office network. The firm invests in early-stage disruptive startups 'building the India of tomorrow', combining technology with measurable impact, and is explicitly values-driven: Jain emphasises integrity and trust as non-negotiables and favours long-term partnerships over quick wins, looking beyond pitch decks to founders' intent and character. Sun Icon writes cheques of roughly $30K to $400K at seed to pre-Series A, with the ability to lead or co-lead and target ownership of 1–15%, supported by senior/technical hiring help, Series A intros and a manufacturing, supply-chain and distribution network. Its interests centre on AI-driven solutions in agriculture, climate and healthcare, plus robotics, drones, IoT, hardware and B2B/enterprise SaaS. Notably, it consciously avoids marketing-heavy consumer brands, saturated generic SaaS and the crowded, tightly-regulated fintech sector. Portfolio companies include drone startup Suind, blockchain firm Dhiway, Omnivio, AjnaLens, agritech CultYvate and vernacular e-learning platform Vidyakul.

investors.name: Neon Fund
investors.thesis: Help Indian B2B SaaS / Enterprise-AI startups go global; act as US go-to-market partner to take companies to $10M ARR in 3–5 years.
investors.notes: Founders Siddhartha Ahluwalia & Nansi Mishra (The Neon Show; ex-100x Entrepreneur). Fund III $25M; Fund IV $50M raising. Delaware LP, US+India. Portfolio: Requestly (acq. BrowserStack), Highperformr, Zepic, Merlin AI.
investors.writeup: Neon Fund is an early-stage venture firm built specifically to help Indian B2B SaaS and enterprise-AI startups go global, founded by Siddhartha Ahluwalia and Nansi Mishra — hosts of the widely followed Neon Show (formerly the 100x Entrepreneur podcast). The fund evolved from their earlier $10–11 million 100x Entrepreneur vehicle, which backed 40+ SaaS startups including Airmeet, Astra Security, CloudSEK, InFeedo and SpotDraft. Neon's third fund stands at $25 million and a fourth fund of $50 million is being raised. It invests at pre-seed and seed, writing cheques of roughly $500K to $1 million, and positions itself as a hands-on go-to-market partner for the US market — helping portfolio companies with demand generation, outbound sales, branding and hiring, with the explicit goal of reaching $10 million in ARR within three to five years. The fund is structured as a Delaware limited partnership operating across the US and India, and its LP base includes CXOs from Amazon, Microsoft and HP, plus prominent SaaS founders and investors like Blume Founders Fund and Nexus's Sandeep Singhal. Recent portfolio companies include Requestly (acquired by BrowserStack), Highperformr, Zepic and Merlin AI. About half its bets back second-time founders, the rest first-timers with strong revenue focus.

investors.name: Pentathlon Ventures
investors.thesis: Founder's fund focused on early-stage Indian B2B SaaS; disciplined use-case-first investing in enterprise software built in India for global markets.
investors.notes: Pune-based, founded 2020 by Gireendra Kasmalkar, Sandeep Chawda, Madhukar Bhatia, Hemant Joshi, Saurabh Lahoti. Fund I ~INR 76–80 Cr (23 cos); Fund II final close INR 255 Cr. Portfolio: OneStack, Vodex, ElevateHQ, Kenko Health, TurboHire, ShopSe.
investors.writeup: Pentathlon Ventures is a Pune-based early-stage venture firm founded in 2020 that focuses exclusively on Indian B2B SaaS, run as a 'founder's fund' by a team of veteran operators including Gireendra Kasmalkar, Sandeep Chawda, Madhukar Bhatia, Hemant Joshi and Saurabh Lahoti — collectively bringing more than 150 years of entrepreneurial and investment experience. Its investment thesis centres on disciplined, use-case-first investing in enterprise software built in India for global markets, spanning enterprise digital transformation, ecommerce enablement, fintech, vertical SaaS, applied AI, sustainable tech, healthtech, cybersecurity and logistics. Fund I closed at roughly INR 76–80 crore ($9.5 million) and backed 23 startups, of which several have crossed $1 million ARR with 8x revenue growth. Fund II, launched in September 2023 with a target of INR 450 crore, reached a final close of INR 255 crore backed by family offices, HNIs and entrepreneurs across India and the US, and aims to back 16–25 companies. Ticket sizes run from about INR 75 lakh to INR 3 crore at pre-seed to Series A in Fund I, rising to roughly INR 4–8 crore in Fund II. Portfolio companies include OneStack, Vodex, ElevateHQ, AyushPay, Kenko Health, TurboHire, Riskcovry and ShopSe. Beyond capital, Pentathlon offers deep enterprise networks and operator mentorship.

investors.name: Alkemi Growth Capital
investors.thesis: India-focused healthcare and wellness fund investing exclusively in scalable companies with validated product-market fit, governance-aligned leadership and a clear pathway to institutional scale; sector specialisation plus long-term partnership capital.
investors.notes: New Delhi. Founded 2017 by Alka Goel (Founder & Managing Partner; Delhi/New York) with Dr. Mansi Aggarwal (Partner); one of few women-led India VCs. Fund I ~$34M AUM, ~20–24 investments. Fund II target $75M (first close $49.7M; IFC up to $10M equity). Portfolio: Redcliffe Labs, Farmley, Jobizo, Akiva Superfoods; exit: Doxper. Healthcare advisory board incl. CEOs of Medanta, Cipla, Swiggy.
investors.writeup: Alkemi Growth Capital is a New Delhi-based, early-growth venture fund focused exclusively on India's healthcare and consumer-wellness sectors, founded in 2017 by Alka Goel, who returned from the US to launch one of the few women-led venture funds in the country. Alongside partner Dr. Mansi Aggarwal and a team drawn from McKinsey, IIM-Ahmedabad and AIIMS, Goel has built Alkemi into a sector-specialist investor backing scalable companies that have validated product-market fit, governance-aligned leadership and a clear pathway to institutional scale. The firm's debut fund holds roughly $34 million in assets and has made around 20 investments, primarily at Series A, with cheque sizes spanning $100K to $5 million and a sweet spot near $1.5 million. It is now raising a second fund targeting $75 million, having reached a first close of about $49.7 million with the IFC committing up to $10 million in equity plus a co-investment envelope — a strong endorsement of its strategy and ESG framework. Portfolio companies include diagnostics chain Redcliffe Labs, healthy-snacking brand Farmley, healthcare-staffing platform Jobizo and Akiva Superfoods, with an exit in Doxper. Alkemi's advisory board features senior healthcare and business leaders, including the CEOs of Medanta, Cipla and Swiggy, reinforcing its operator and clinical network.

investors.name: WEIN Capital
investors.thesis: Accelerate Indian new-age consumer brands — helping micro-businesses and product/brand owners grow reach across online and offline retail via an omni-channel approach, plus fundraising support; enters at the product-market-fit stage.
investors.notes: India. Nascent investor/accelerator for new-age consumer/D2C brands (also weinpe.com). Founding partners are first-generation consumer-goods operators with D2C toy & gifting backgrounds; one co-founded Rowboat, a founders-and-investors community (2022). Limited public disclosure on fund size, cheque size and portfolio.
investors.writeup: WEIN Capital is an early-stage, India-focused investor and accelerator concentrating on new-age consumer brands. Its stated mission is to help micro-businesses, product makers and D2C brand owners 'go from zero to one' — entering at the product-market-fit stage and accelerating growth by expanding a brand's reach across both online channels and physical retail through an omni-channel distribution approach, while also supporting founders in raising capital. The firm is run by first-generation founders and operators with hands-on experience in the consumer-goods sector, including a D2C toy-and-gifting business; one founding partner also established Rowboat, a community launched in 2022 that connects founders and investors. WEIN positions itself around speed, low cost and growth for the brands it backs, and frames the next decade as 'India's decade' for consumer entrepreneurship. Public disclosure on the firm is currently limited — fund size, typical cheque size and a named portfolio are not publicly available — so this profile is intentionally conservative and will be expanded as verified details emerge. (Note: distinct from WEH Ventures, a separate Mumbai seed fund listed elsewhere in this sheet.)

investors.name: Warmup Ventures
investors.thesis: Founders-led, sector-agnostic technology micro-VC backing high-quality teams identified through 'green signals'; bridge India's business heritage — family offices and second-generation entrepreneurs — with future-forward startups, offering networks, GTM and hiring help beyond capital.
investors.notes: Jaipur. Founded mid-2023 (syndicate, then institutional fund). Team ~10 incl 4 partners. Fund II INR 300 Cr launched Dec 2024, targeting 25–30 startups with follow-on reserves. 15–23 investments: Bobabhai, Nitro Commerce, Balwaan Krishi, MiniMines, RocketPay, DATOMS, GreenStitch, DrinkPrime, Chakr Innovation.
investors.writeup: Warmup Ventures is a Jaipur-based, founders-led micro-VC firm that began in mid-2023 as a syndicate before scaling into an institutional fund. Sector-agnostic but technology-focused, it invests at pre-seed and seed, placing particular emphasis on 'green signals' that indicate high-quality founding teams. The firm's partners — a team of around ten including four partners — have themselves walked the founder's path of scaling businesses, raising capital and building teams, and they position Warmup as more than a cheque: portfolio companies get help with introductions to follow-on investors, connections to CEOs of large tech companies for business synergies, go-to-market planning and key technical hires. A distinctive part of its thesis is bridging India's traditional business heritage with its innovation economy by connecting family offices and second-generation entrepreneurs with future-forward startups. In December 2024 Warmup launched a ₹300 crore second fund, aiming to deploy roughly ₹5–7 crore into each of 25–30 early-stage startups with reserves for follow-on rounds. It has backed more than fifteen companies to date, including bubble-tea chain Bobabhai (expanded to 45 stores), Nitro Commerce, agri-equipment brand Balwaan Krishi, battery-recycling startup MiniMines, RocketPay and industrial-IoT platform DATOMS, with several having gone on to raise larger rounds — evidence of its early-conviction model.

investors.name: Aureolis Ventures
investors.thesis: Partner with global teams on a mission to solve the world's most important problems; founder-first, impact-oriented investing with gender-lens principles, prioritising defensible IP and scalable models.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2017 by Paula Mariwala — one of India's first women VCs, founder of Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs India, ex-MD Seedfund. Co-founders incl. Jo Pattabiraman, Ruchi Jain Hanasoge. Team ~12. Portfolio 49 cos, 1 unicorn (Unacademy); notable: Fasal, Unbox Robotics, Zyla Health. Active in gender-lens investing; Paula's broader exits incl. RedBus, Carwale, TapChief.
investors.writeup: Aureolis Ventures is a Mumbai-based early-stage venture firm founded in 2017 by Paula Mariwala, one of the pioneering women venture capitalists in India. A Stanford-educated physicist and technologist, Mariwala has been shaping the country's startup ecosystem since 2006 — she is the founder and President Emeritus of Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs India, the former Managing Director of Seedfund (one of India's first venture funds), and a promoter director of the Hinditron Group. Aureolis partners with global teams on a mission to solve significant problems, focusing on climate change, health, deep tech, education and consumer, and invests across pre-seed, seed and Series A. The firm takes a founder-first, impact-oriented approach and is an active participant in gender-lens investing, looking beyond female founders to companies whose products and workplaces benefit women. Its portfolio spans 49 companies, including the unicorn Unacademy, alongside agritech firm Fasal, warehouse-robotics company Unbox Robotics and digital-health platform Zyla Health. Mariwala's broader 25-year investing career includes notable exits such as RedBus, Carwale and TapChief, giving her deep experience across the full venture lifecycle from sourcing to exit. Backed by a small, hands-on team of around twelve including co-founders Jo Pattabiraman and Ruchi Jain Hanasoge, Aureolis offers portfolio founders close mentorship and access to global networks to help them scale with impact.

investors.name: Mapleblock Capital
investors.thesis: Exclusively back early-stage blockchain and Web3 founders 'who can code the future', providing capital plus a robust support system and crypto-native networks to help projects launch, build communities and scale.
investors.notes: Delhi. Founded 2017; exclusively crypto-assets & blockchain. Reported 38–150+ Web3 investments across stages. Portfolio: Ankr, Elrond/MultiversX, MANTRA, Polyhedra Network, Good Games Guild, READYgg, Kawaii Islands (lead), Mara. Co-invests with Hashed, Polychain, Animoca Brands, Coinbase Ventures. (Note: previously-listed founder name and website could not be verified and were removed.)
investors.writeup: Mapleblock Capital is a Delhi-based investment firm founded in 2017 that focuses exclusively on crypto-assets and blockchain companies, making it one of India's earliest crypto-native venture investors. The firm invests across the early stages of the Web3 lifecycle — including seed rounds, strategic rounds and token sales — backing founders it describes as those who 'can code the future' and supplementing capital with a hands-on support system spanning technical resources, community building, token strategy and access to a global crypto network. Its partners are experienced operators in the crypto and blockchain sectors who leverage extensive industry relationships to add value. Mapleblock has built a broad portfolio — reported across sources at anywhere from several dozen to well over a hundred Web3 projects — with notable investments including infrastructure protocol Ankr, Layer-1 network Elrond (now MultiversX), MANTRA, zero-knowledge interoperability project Polyhedra Network, Good Games Guild, Web3-gaming firm READYgg and play-to-earn game Kawaii Islands, where it served as lead investor. It frequently co-invests alongside leading global crypto funds such as Hashed, Polychain Capital, Animoca Brands and Coinbase Ventures. Sitting at the intersection of India's deep developer talent pool and the global Web3 opportunity, Mapleblock is positioned as a strategic partner for blockchain founders targeting worldwide markets.
investors.confidence: Verified (web sources, 2025) – some details vary across sources

investors.name: Sixth Sense Ventures
investors.thesis: India's first domestic consumer-centric fund — 'invest in the Consumer of Tomorrow, Today'; back first-generation entrepreneurs disrupting large, sticky consumer categories with differentiated skill sets rather than just capital.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded ~2014 by Nikhil Vora (ex-MD & Head of Research, IDFC Securities; India's #1 analyst 2012). AUM $150M+, ~23 investments, ~40% IRR. Funds: SSIO I (INR 118 Cr), SSIO II (INR 515 Cr). Ranked top-5 India VC by Preqin (SSIO II #3, SSIO I #5). Portfolio: Bombay Shaving Company, Cult.fit, Purplle, Wonderchef, ETHOS, INDICOLD, Bewakoof.
investors.writeup: Sixth Sense Ventures is India's first domestic, consumer-focused venture capital fund, founded around 2014 by Nikhil Vora, the former Managing Director and Head of Research at IDFC Securities who was voted India's number-one analyst in 2012. Built on Vora's three-decade study of Indian consumer and finance markets, the fund's philosophy is to 'invest in the Consumer of Tomorrow, Today' — backing first-generation entrepreneurs disrupting large, sticky consumer categories through differentiated capability rather than capital alone. Headquartered in Mumbai, Sixth Sense has grown to over $150 million in assets under management across two funds, with around 23 investments and a reported IRR near 40%. Its first fund (SSIO I) raised INR 118 crore, while its second (SSIO II) closed at INR 515 crore — more than double its INR 250 crore target — in a record nine months; both funds have been ranked among the top five Indian venture firms of the past decade by Preqin. The fund typically invests $1–5 million per company across consumer, FMCG, retail, D2C and food and beverage. Its portfolio includes Bombay Shaving Company, Cult.fit, Purplle, Wonderchef, luxury-watch retailer ETHOS, INDICOLD and Bewakoof. Beyond capital, Sixth Sense leverages a deep consumer ecosystem — distribution, branding and FMCG networks — to help founders scale, making it the preferred partner for consumer businesses in India.

investors.name: VeritasX
investors.thesis: A New Delhi venture firm of business owners, entrepreneurs, professionals and strategists with two decades-plus of industry experience, backing early-stage founders — often co-investing alongside angel networks and seed funds.
investors.notes: New Delhi. Founded 2021; small team. Two disclosed seed investments: Jobizo and Mykare Health ($2.01M seed, Jun 2023), co-investing with Aroa Venture Partners, Avaana, OnDeck, Stanford Angels & Huddle Ventures. Limited public data on fund size/cheque. (Distinct from Veritas Capital (US) and Veritas Venture Partners (Israel).)
investors.writeup: VeritasX is an early-stage venture capital firm based in New Delhi, founded in 2021 by a group of business owners, entrepreneurs, professionals and strategists who collectively bring more than two decades of industry experience. The firm invests at the seed stage in India-based startups, with its disclosed activity concentrated in healthtech and business-services. Public records show a small, focused footprint — two named investments to date: healthcare-staffing platform Jobizo and Mykare Health, the latter a roughly $2.01 million seed round in June 2023 in which VeritasX participated alongside a broad syndicate including Aroa Venture Partners, Avaana Capital, OnDeck, Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs and Huddle Ventures. Beyond this, the firm keeps a low public profile: its fund size, typical cheque size and a fuller portfolio are not publicly disclosed, so this profile is intentionally conservative and would benefit from primary confirmation. It should not be confused with the similarly named Veritas Capital (a large US private-equity firm) or Veritas Venture Partners (an Israeli VC), which are unrelated entities.

investors.name: BlueGreen Ventures
investors.thesis: Two-pronged strategy: lead early-stage rounds in climate/sustainability, fintech for 'new India' and post-Covid B2C consumption; plus selective secondary investments in IPO-ready growth companies to deliver faster liquidity to LPs.
investors.notes: Founded 2024 by Rajeev Suri & Anup Jain, both former Managing Partners at Orios Venture Partners. Maiden fund $75M (~INR 633 Cr, + green-shoe), launched Nov 2024, first close ~Feb 2025. Targets ~20 startups, leads rounds. Prior track record (Suri/Jain): BatterySmart, Zupee, Ixigo, Varaha, Beato, Karbon — 60%+ IRR (2018–21). Climate advisor: Sophie Lambin.
investors.writeup: BlueGreen Ventures is an early-stage India venture fund launched in November 2024 by Rajeev Suri and Anup Jain, two operators-turned-investors who previously served as Managing Partners at Orios Venture Partners. Their maiden vehicle targets $75 million (about ₹633 crore) with a green-shoe option, reaching its first close in early 2025. BlueGreen runs a distinctive two-pronged strategy. Its primary pillar leads early-stage rounds, from seed to Series A, in high-impact sectors — climate and sustainability, fintech solutions tailored for 'new India', and consumer-driven B2C businesses reflecting post-Covid consumption shifts — writing cheques of ₹7–12 crore and aiming to lead every such round while working closely with founders. Its second pillar selectively backs mature, IPO-ready companies via secondary investments of ₹20–30 crore, targeting businesses valued around $250 million expected to go public within four to five years, which offers LPs liquidity on a shorter five-year horizon. The fund plans a focused portfolio of roughly 20 startups. Suri and Jain bring a strong prior track record — investments including Battery Smart, Zupee, ixigo, carbon-removal startup Varaha, Beato and Karbon, with reported IRRs above 60% between 2018 and 2021 — and have appointed climate expert Sophie Lambin as a strategic advisor to reinforce sustainability investing.

investors.name: Disruptors Capital
investors.thesis: Founder-dedicated early-stage fund that supplements capital with hands-on strategic guidance — business model, product thinking and go-to-market — to bridge the structural gaps first-time founders face when raising institutional rounds; backs high-LTV tech companies at the cutting edge of cross-sector innovation.
investors.notes: New Delhi/Bengaluru (+US). Founded 2021 by Raj Snehil Juneja (ex-Khetal Advisors; worked with ~500 startups buy- and sell-side). SEBI Cat-I AIF, INR 120 Cr; invests across India, SE Asia and US Bay Area. ~9–17 investments. Portfolio: Apna Mart, Biofuels Junction, Purple Tutor, Playto Labs. Fund partner Krishna Kumar (Simplilearn CEO).
investors.writeup: Disruptors Capital is a founder-dedicated, early-stage venture capital fund based across New Delhi and Bengaluru (with a US presence), founded in 2021 by Raj Snehil Juneja. Juneja came to investing from the advisory side — having worked with around 500 startups and run fundraising and M&A transactions at Khetal Advisors — and built Disruptors after observing that strong founders often struggle to raise institutional rounds because of structural gaps and a lack of early guidance. The firm secured SEBI approval in early 2022 to launch a ₹120 crore Category-I Alternative Investment Fund, which invests in technology startups across India, South-East Asia and the US Bay Area. It focuses primarily on seed-stage, high-LTV technology companies at the intersection of cross-sector innovation, led by high-quality founding teams, with named sector emphasis on edtech, fintech, health tech and enterprise technologies. Beyond capital, Disruptors leans on the experience of seasoned operators — including fund partner Krishna Kumar, CEO of Simplilearn — to help portfolio founders refine business models, sharpen product thinking and build go-to-market strategies. Its portfolio of roughly 9–17 companies includes quick-commerce grocery startup Apna Mart, clean-energy marketplace Biofuels Junction, coding-education platform Purple Tutor and Playto Labs. The firm is deliberately founder-first, positioning itself as a hands-on early partner rather than purely a capital provider.

investors.name: 8X Ventures
investors.thesis: DeepTech-focused VC backing startups with strong scientific and research foundations that can fundamentally transform industries and economies; invests and enables, leveraging Middle East and Europe relationships to help portfolio companies expand globally and raise larger follow-on rounds.
investors.chequeSize: Initial INR 2–5 Cr; up to ~INR 20 Cr incl. follow-on
investors.notes: Chennai. Founded 2021 by Chirag Gupta (Managing Partner). Fund I (2022, ~$24M AUM) reportedly 2.1x with 40%+ annual return. Fund II: INR 200 Cr DeepTech fund (+INR 100 Cr green-shoe), first close 2025; plans 18–20 startups over 3 years. Portfolio: Solinas Integrity, Pantherun, Xyma Analytics, LightSpeed Photonics, Enerzi. MENA & Europe network for global scale. (Website is 8xventures.co.)
investors.writeup: 8X Ventures is a Chennai-based, deep-tech-focused venture capital firm founded in 2021 and led by Managing Partner Chirag Gupta. The fund backs early-stage startups built on strong scientific and research foundations — companies it believes can address major global problems and fundamentally transform industries and economies. Its focus areas span water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), Industry 4.0, advanced and quantum computing, biotech, and B2B enterprise SaaS, with broader exposure to cleantech, smart logistics and mobility, robotics, AI, big data, 3D printing and IoT. While rooted in India, 8X leverages close relationships across the Middle East and Europe to help portfolio companies expand internationally and attract regional investors for larger follow-on rounds. Its first fund, launched in 2022 with around $24 million, has reportedly returned about 2.1x with a 40%-plus annual return rate. In 2025 the firm announced the first close of a second fund — a ₹200 crore deep-tech vehicle with an option to add another ₹100 crore — through which it plans to back 18–20 early-stage startups over three years, writing initial cheques of ₹2–5 crore and deploying up to roughly ₹20 crore per company including follow-on. Portfolio companies include robotics-and-sanitation innovator Solinas Integrity, Pantherun, Xyma Analytics, LightSpeed Photonics and Enerzi.

investors.name: Silverneedle Ventures
investors.companyTypeRaw: VC (early-stage, sector-agnostic with deep-tech lean; SEBI AIF)
investors.thesis: Hands-on, active early-stage investor partnering with entrepreneurs to increase their probability of success; backs India-first companies with global ambitions, with a special focus on deep technology, sustainability and emerging technologies.
investors.notes: Hyderabad (T-Hub, Madhapur). Founded 2022 by Ajay Jain & Deepesh Agarwal (previously ran Xseed Partners — 5 yrs, 25 startups). SEBI-approved Aug 2022. Fund I INR 100 Cr (~$12–15M), target 30 startups in 18 months, 3–5 yr exit horizon; also launched SilverX deep-tech fund (~INR 800 Cr / ~$95M). ~15–29 investments, ~8 exits; team of 14 incl 4 partners. Portfolio: Knorish (first deal), Disprz, Hypergro.ai, BrainSightAI, Dhruva Space.
investors.writeup: Silverneedle Ventures is a Hyderabad-based early-stage venture capital firm founded in 2022 by Ajay Jain and Deepesh Agarwal, who previously ran their first fund, Xseed Partners, for five years and backed 25 startups. Operating out of T-Hub in Madhapur and approved by SEBI in August 2022, the firm describes itself as a hands-on, active investor that partners closely with entrepreneurs to raise their probability of success. It is broadly sector-agnostic but maintains a special focus on deep technology, sustainability and emerging technologies, alongside B2B, SaaS, D2C/consumer-internet and edtech, emphasising India-first companies with global ambitions that can expand into Southeast Asia and the Middle East. Its maiden fund is sized at around ₹100 crore (roughly $12–15 million), with a plan to back about 30 startups in 18 months at ₹1–6 crore per deal and support them through exits typically targeted within three to five years; the firm has since launched a much larger deep-tech vehicle, the SilverX Fund, reportedly around ₹800 crore. To date Silverneedle has screened hundreds of startups and made roughly 15–29 investments with several exits, supported by a team of about 14 including four partners. Portfolio companies include creator-monetisation platform Knorish, learning platform Disprz, AI-video-marketing startup Hypergro, neuroscience firm BrainSightAI and Dhruva Space.

investors.name: Precog Innovation Partners
investors.companyTypeRaw: Venture-building / Co-creation platform (CleanTech) — makes strategic investments, JVs, acquisitions
investors.thesis: Cross-border co-creation and venture-building platform focused on decarbonising key industry sectors for India's Net-Zero transition; connect 30+ large Indian business groups with global climate-tech ventures to enable their India market entry, build-out and scale-up.
investors.chequeSize: Not disclosed (strategic investments, JVs, licensing, mfg/distribution agreements)
investors.notes: Gurugram/Kolkata. Founded 2017 by Sumit Dhanuka (Founder & Managing Partner). Cleantech venture-building/co-creation platform; works with 30+ Indian business groups (Precog Family Business Network) and 15+ global innovation ecosystems (US, Europe, SE Asia, ANZ, Canada, Israel). ~16 portfolio cos; notable: AirOK Technologies; outcomes incl. 1 IPO and 2 acquisitions (Linkker, Emuron, Climate Connect). Not a conventional cheque-writing VC fund.
investors.writeup: Precog Innovation Partners is a cross-border co-creation and venture-building platform founded in 2017 and based across Gurugram and Kolkata, led by Founder and Managing Partner Sumit Dhanuka. Rather than operating as a conventional cheque-writing venture fund, Precog positions itself as a catalyst for India's Net-Zero transition, focused on decarbonising key industrial sectors. Its core themes span Net-Zero energy, mobility, building and construction, circular economy and advanced materials. The platform's distinctive model connects a network of more than 30 large Indian business groups — its 'Family Business Network' — with mission-driven global climate-technology ventures and entrepreneurial talent, fast-tracking those corporates' growth, diversification and decarbonisation goals through long-term co-creation partnerships. These collaborations can take varied forms, including strategic investments, strategic acquisitions, joint ventures, technology licensing, and manufacturing and distribution agreements. Precog works with 15-plus innovation-led ecosystems across the US, Europe, Southeast Asia, ANZ, Canada and Israel, and provides ventures with strategic access to capital, talent, distribution networks and manufacturing and supply-chain support to enter and scale in the Indian market. Its portfolio spans around 16 companies — with air-purification firm AirOK Technologies among the most notable — and it has recorded outcomes including an IPO and two acquisitions across names such as Linkker, Emuron and Climate Connect.

investors.name: growX ventures
investors.thesis: Thesis-driven, patient-capital investor backing founders solving foundational problems with deep science and engineering; betting on India building globally competitive deep-tech products.
investors.notes: New Delhi-based, founded 2008 (Fund I 2018) by Ashish Taneja & Sheetal Bahl. Fund II ~INR 400 Cr ($50M). Portfolio: Pixxel (17x partial exit), Locus, Bellatrix Aerospace, CynLr, Stashfin, Progcap, RACE Energy.
investors.writeup: growX ventures is a New Delhi-based, thesis-driven venture firm and one of India's most committed deep-technology investors. Tracing its roots to 2008 and launching its first SEBI-registered fund in 2018, it is led by founder Ashish Taneja with managing director Sheetal Bahl and general partner Manish Gupta. growX backs founders solving foundational, often overlooked problems using cutting-edge science and engineering, treating deep tech as a mindset rather than a sector. Its portfolio of roughly 48–58 companies spans space tech, defence, semiconductors, robotics, genomics, AI, cybersecurity, EVs, B2B SaaS and fintech, and includes standout names such as Pixxel — from which growX booked a 17x partial exit at a 68% IRR over 5.5 years — alongside Locus, Bellatrix Aerospace, CynLr, Stashfin, Progcap, Aereo and RACE Energy. Fund I deployed across 17 investments, eight of them deep tech. Fund II carries a target corpus of INR 400 crore (about $50 million), with roughly a quarter allocated to seed rounds and the remainder reserved for follow-on through Series B; cheque sizes reach up to INR 10 crore at seed and INR 20–30 crore at Series B, supporting 20–24 startups over the fund's life. growX champions patient capital and hands-on mentorship for India's frontier-tech founders.

investors.name: YourNest Venture Capital
investors.companyTypeRaw: VC (early-stage / Pre-Series A, DeepTech & B2B; SEBI AIF)
investors.thesis: Nurture global market leaders from India by backing product-led, IP-backed DeepTech and enterprise (B2B) founders; a horizontal partnership model with a high partner-to-founder ratio, concentrating efforts on a handful of companies for long-term success.
investors.notes: Gurugram. Founded 2011 by Sunil K Goyal (MD & Fund Manager; partners incl. Girish Shivani, Sanjay Pande). Three funds: Fund I (2012, $14M/INR 90 Cr, 16 cos; exits Uniphore, SmartQ; returned ~70% of corpus); Fund II (2017, $30M/INR 215 Cr, 19 DeepTech cos — Miko, Dozee, Exponent Energy); Fund III ($69M, anchored by sovereign fund NIIF). Cumulative AUM ~$53M valued ~$1.2bn (May 2025). 58 cos, 1 unicorn (Uniphore), 9 acquisitions.
investors.writeup: YourNest Venture Capital is a Gurugram-based, early-stage fund established in 2011 to nurture global market leaders from India, led by Managing Director and Fund Manager Sunil K Goyal. Sharply focused on the 'Pre-Series A' stage, it backs product-led, IP-backed startups in DeepTech — spanning AI, IoT, robotics, space tech, quantum computing, AR/VR/MR, edge cloud and health tech — alongside enterprise (B2B) software. The firm has built a thesis around India's shift from an IT-services outsourcing hub to an IP- and patent-driven 'Product Nation', and operates a distinctive horizontal partnership model with a high partner-to-founder ratio, deliberately investing in a small number of founders and concentrating its efforts on each. YourNest has launched three funds roughly every five years: Fund I (2012, ~$14M, 16 companies, with exits including Uniphore and SmartQ returning much of the corpus); Fund II (2017, ~$30M/₹215 crore, 19 deep-tech startups such as Miko, Dozee and Exponent Energy); and Fund III, a ~$69M vehicle anchored by India's sovereign National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF). Its three funds carry a cumulative AUM of about $53 million valued near $1.2 billion as of May 2025, across 58 companies that include one unicorn — conversational-AI leader Uniphore — and nine acquisitions, with the firm targeting ₹2,000 crore in AUM over the next three years.

investors.name: Venture Catalysts | India's First Integrated Incubator
investors.companyTypeRaw: Integrated Incubator + Angel Network / Multi-stage VC (VCats Group)
investors.thesis: India's first integrated incubator — combine capital, mentoring and network to write early external cheques for nascent startups; syndicate deals with HNIs, family offices and CXOs, and provide ~3 months of acceleration plus ~18 months of post-investment support.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2015 by Apoorv Ranjan Sharma, Anuj Golecha, Anil Jain & Gaurav Jain. India's first & largest integrated incubator/angel network; 10,000+ angels & family offices; present across 31 Indian cities + UAE, US, UK, Singapore; curates 600+ deals/month. Flagship accelerator fund: 100Unicorns (formerly 9Unicorns). Portfolio: BharatPe, Fynd, Beardo, Pee Safe, Klub, Shiprocket, Zypp Electric, BluSmart, Niyo. 45+ global co-investors; 35+ multibagger exits.
investors.writeup: Venture Catalysts is India's first and largest integrated incubator and angel network, founded in 2015 by Apoorv Ranjan Sharma, Anuj Golecha, Anil Jain and Gaurav Jain, and headquartered in Mumbai. It pioneered a model that combines capital, mentoring and network on a single platform — pooling money from a community of more than 10,000 angel investors, HNIs and family offices to write early external cheques for nascent startups. The firm typically invests $275K to $2 million in early-stage companies through syndicated rounds, and provides every portfolio company roughly three months of acceleration support followed by around 18 months of post-investment guidance, with scope for follow-on cheques of ₹3–5 crore for those showing sustained promise. Venture Catalysts curates more than 600 deals a month and operates across 31 Indian cities and four countries (UAE, US, UK and Singapore). Its flagship accelerator fund, 100Unicorns (formerly 9Unicorns), institutionalises idea-stage seed capital at scale. The group's portfolio includes category leaders such as BharatPe, Fynd, Beardo, Pee Safe, Klub, Shiprocket, Zypp Electric, BluSmart and Niyo, and it has attracted more than 45 international Grade-A co-investors — including Google, Accel, Sequoia, Bain Capital and Y Combinator — while delivering 35-plus multibagger exits over five years.

investors.name: Sangam Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest to improve access to sustainable energy and resource-productivity solutions for the underserved in India; back solutions that drive inclusive development and build communities resilient to climate change, starting small and growing alongside portfolio companies with hands-on, operator-first support.
investors.chequeSize: Seed / early-stage cheques (small initial, scaling with companies)
investors.notes: Gurugram/New Delhi (Chattarpur). Founded 2016 (entity since 2012) by Karthik Chandrasekar (IIT-Bombay; ex-TVS Capital, Ventureast, Acumen). ~19–20 investments, 50+ deals; team ~35 incl 13 partners. Portfolio: Inficold, Promethean Energy, Smart Joules, Cell Propulsion, Carbon Masters/Carbonlites. Runs AIC Sangam (CleanTech incubator with Atal Innovation Mission). Network/LPs incl. IFC, Aavishkaar, GIZ, Bharat Innovation Fund.
investors.writeup: Sangam Ventures is a seed and early-stage venture fund based in Gurugram/New Delhi, founded by Karthik Chandrasekar, who developed his interest in climate and cleantech during his B.Tech years at IIT-Bombay and learned venture investing at TVS Capital Funds, Ventureast and the impact fund Acumen before starting Sangam around 2016. The fund's mission is to improve access to sustainable energy and resource-productivity solutions for the underserved in India, backing solutions that drive inclusive development and build communities resilient to climate change. Its focus spans cleantech, energy tech, climate and environment tech, and food and agriculture tech. Reflecting Chandrasekar's Acumen-shaped philosophy that early-stage entrepreneurship needs 'something beyond the money', Sangam takes a hands-on, operator-first approach, deliberately starting with small cheques and growing alongside its portfolio companies — appropriate for cleantech businesses that don't require large capital at inception. The firm has made around 19–20 investments across 50-plus deals, supported by a team of roughly 35 including 13 partners, with notable portfolio companies including thermal-battery cooling firm Inficold, Promethean Energy, energy-efficiency company Smart Joules, Cell Propulsion and Carbon Masters. Sangam also runs AIC Sangam, a cleantech incubator in partnership with the Atal Innovation Mission, and counts IFC, Aavishkaar, GIZ and Bharat Innovation Fund among its ecosystem partners.

investors.name: Bharat Innovation Fund
investors.companyTypeRaw: VC (deep-tech thematic, SEBI Cat-I AIF; part of CIIE.CO / IIM Ahmedabad)
investors.thesis: Back IP-driven deep-tech founders building 'companies of consequence' that remain outside most VCs' deal flow at inception; as high-touch investors, lead founders in the right direction and help de-risk technology, regulatory and execution risk over long gestation periods, providing network, customers and resources.
investors.chequeSize: Initially INR 3–15 Cr (BIF); INR 2–6 Cr (Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund)
investors.notes: Ahmedabad. Founded 2018 under CIIE.CO at IIM Ahmedabad; co-founder Ashwin Raguraman (earlier India Innovation Fund, 2010). $100M corpus split across Bharat Innovation Fund + Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund. 27 investments; 1 unicorn (CRED), 2 acquisitions (Setu, Prefr). Portfolio: PlayShifu, Entropik Tech, CreditVidya, Detect Technologies, vPhrase, Portl, Optimized Electrotech, Virohan. LPs incl. SIDBI FoF, ICICI Lombard, SBI Life, RBL Bank, Federal Bank. Fund II planned.
investors.writeup: Bharat Innovation Fund (BIF) is an Ahmedabad-based, deep-tech-focused venture firm launched in 2018 under the aegis of CIIE.CO, the Centre for Innovation, Incubation and Entrepreneurship continuum at IIM Ahmedabad, and co-founded by Ashwin Raguraman, who had earlier run the India Innovation Fund. A SEBI Category-I AIF with a $100 million corpus — allocated across BIF and the sister Bharat Inclusion Seed Fund — it was created specifically to back IP-driven deep-tech and breakthrough-innovation startups that typically fall outside most VCs' profiles and deal flow at the earliest stages, where the first product is expensive and slow to build. BIF invests across Seed to Series B, with initial cheques generally between ₹3 and ₹15 crore, in sectors spanning AI, AR/VR, IoT, machine learning and big data applied to healthcare, agriculture, renewable energy and advanced technology; the Inclusion Seed Fund writes ₹2–6 crore into India-Stack-based products for the next billion users. As high-touch investors, the team focuses on de-risking technology, regulatory and execution challenges over long gestation cycles. Its portfolio of around 27 companies includes PlayShifu, Entropik Tech, CreditVidya, Detect Technologies, Portl, Optimized Electrotech and Virohan, with one unicorn (CRED) and acquisitions in Setu and Prefr. Its institutional LPs include SIDBI's Fund of Funds, ICICI Lombard, SBI Life, RBL Bank and Federal Bank, and a second fund is planned.

investors.name: Omnivore
investors.thesis: Back entrepreneurs building breakthrough technologies for agriculture, food, climate and the rural economy that deliver disproportionate impact on the lives of farmers and rural communities in India and Southeast Asia; conviction that Indian agritech companies are 'built to last'.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2010 by Mark Kahn & Jinesh Shah — India's first dedicated agritech VC; partners Reihem Roy & Subhadeep Sanyal; team ~18 incl 4–5 partners. Three funds + ACSF; cumulative AUM ~$700M+. Fund III (Agritech & Climate Sustainability Fund) first close $150M (launched Apr 2022), 25–30 investments planned. 57–59 cos, 5 exits. Portfolio: DeHaat, Ecozen, Pixxel, Stellapps, Varaha, Tractor Junction, Loopworm. DFI LPs: IFC, KfW, FMO, Proparco, Gates Foundation, Louis Dreyfus, Yara, SIFEM, SRI Fund.
investors.writeup: Omnivore is India's pioneering agrifood and climate-focused impact venture firm, founded in 2010 in Mumbai by Mark Kahn and Jinesh Shah as the country's first dedicated agritech VC — Kahn having previously been EVP of Strategy and Business Development at Godrej Agrovet. Alongside partners Reihem Roy and Subhadeep Sanyal and an 18-person team, Omnivore backs early-stage founders building breakthrough technologies across farmer platforms, agri-fintech, precision agriculture, farm-to-consumer brands, post-harvest and supply-chain tech, and agrifood life sciences, investing across seed to Series A (occasionally Series B) in India and Southeast Asia. The firm has built roughly $700 million in cumulative AUM across three funds plus its Agritech & Climate Sustainability Fund. Its third fund reached a first close of $150 million in 2023 (launched April 2022), backed by a deep development-finance LP base including IFC, KfW, FMO, Proparco, SIFEM, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Louis Dreyfus Company Ventures and Yara Growth Ventures, and plans 25–30 new investments at initial cheques of roughly $1–5 million, with a sharper focus on life sciences and climate resilience. Across 57-plus investments and five exits, its portfolio includes DeHaat, climate-smart deeptech firm Ecozen, space-tech company Pixxel, dairy-tech firm Stellapps, carbon-removal startup Varaha and Tractor Junction — collectively touching over 12 million smallholder farmers.

investors.name: Elevar Equity
investors.thesis: Fuel the economic resilience of underserved low-income customers and 'Entrepreneurial Households' by investing at the intersection of inclusivity, affordability and scale; deliver measurable impact alongside financial returns via the proprietary 'Elevar Method'.
investors.notes: Bengaluru (+US). Founded 2008. Leadership: Johanna Posada (Founder & MP), Jyotsna Krishnan (MP), partners Vipul Rawal, Amie Patel, Shobha Venkataraman; team ~29 incl 8 partners. 5 funds, ~$400M AUM; Fund V (Elevar India V) target $225M (first close $126M), SME-focused. 47–56 investments; 3 unicorns, 2 IPOs (Ujjivan SFB, Bharat Financial Inclusion), 9 acquisitions. Impacted 50M+ households, ~70,000 jobs, 20M women borrowers. Portfolio: Ujjivan SFB, InCred, Varthana, Aye Finance, TapFin, Hippo Stores. Cross-border (India + LatAm).
investors.writeup: Elevar Equity is a Bengaluru-headquartered impact venture firm, founded in 2008, that invests at the intersection of inclusivity, affordability and scale to fuel the economic resilience of underserved low-income customers and what it calls 'Entrepreneurial Households'. Over a 15-plus-year journey it has raised five funds, manages roughly $400 million in AUM, and has catalysed billions in follow-on capital while serving more than 50 million households — supporting around 70,000 jobs and providing loans to some 20 million women borrowers. Its investment themes span financial inclusion, education, healthcare, agri-supply chains and MSME solutions, typically at seed to Series A. The firm's latest vehicle, Elevar India V, targets $225 million and reached a first close of about $126 million, backed by development-finance investors such as British International Investment, focusing on early-stage SMEs delivering essential goods and services. Led by Founder and Managing Partner Johanna Posada and Managing Partner Jyotsna Krishnan, with a 29-person team including eight partners, Elevar applies its proprietary 'Elevar Method' to back businesses serving marginalised customers. Across roughly 56 investments it has produced three unicorns, two IPOs — notably Ujjivan Small Finance Bank and Bharat Financial Inclusion — and nine acquisitions, with portfolio names including InCred, Varthana, Aye Finance, TapFin and Hippo Stores; the firm also invests across India and Latin America.

investors.name: RealTime (RTAF)
investors.thesis: Collaborate with future change-makers to build and scale impact startups; a curated accelerator program designed to bring the best out of seed to pre-series startups, backing 'revolutionary founders building from Bharat to the world' with capital, mentorship and operational support.
investors.notes: Jaipur (legal name Real Time Accelerator LLP). Founded 2020 (2022-vintage fund). SEBI-registered angel fund. GP Amit Singal; GP Dr Vibhuti Aggarwal; IC member Sandeep Bansal. 750+ angel investor community; 34–40+ startups. Runs a curated accelerator (seed–pre-series). Portfolio: MentorKart, MyWays.ai, MyMandi, Stylox, Innoctive, Pantherun (Series A $12M), Burgerama, CargoFL.
investors.writeup: RealTime — formally the Real Time Angel Fund (RTAF), operating through Real Time Accelerator LLP — is a SEBI-registered angel fund based in Jaipur, founded in 2020 and led by General Partner Amit Singal alongside General Partner Dr. Vibhuti Aggarwal and investment-committee member Sandeep Bansal. Its mission is to collaborate with 'future change-makers' to build and scale impact startups, and it pairs capital with a curated accelerator program designed specifically for seed to pre-series companies, layering in mentorship and operational support. RTAF is sector-agnostic with a focus on healthtech, fintech, green energy, artificial intelligence and consumer technology, and typically writes cheques of ₹1–2 crore per startup at pre-seed, seed and pre-Series A. The fund has built a community of more than 750 angel investors and has backed over 34–40 startups, often serving founders building from 'Bharat to the world', including those in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. Its portfolio includes career-tech platform MentorKart, AI HR-tech startup MyWays.ai, B2B agri-marketplace MyMandi, fashion app Stylox, Innoctive, logistics firm CargoFL and food brand Burgerama; notably, portfolio company Pantherun Technologies went on to raise a $12 million Series A in late 2025. Beyond funding, RTAF emphasises active mentorship, ecosystem connections and follow-on fundraising support for its founders.

investors.name: Elev8 Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Back profitable, product-market-fit growth-stage tech companies expanding via overseas expansion, inorganic acquisition, tech-team and CXO hiring or pre-IPO scaling; a research- and data-driven, hands-on partnership model. India's first 'Pro Rata' fund, accessing oversubscribed rounds of top tech companies alongside top-tier growth funds.
investors.notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2022 by Navin Honagudi (ex-Kae Capital partner, 10+ yrs; 50+ investments incl Paytm/Shiprocket/Vedantu) & Abhisekh Shah. $200M fund (debut close ~$160M), SEBI Cat-II AIF + green-shoe; 12–14 investments planned. Anchored by KB Investment (South Korea's KB Group, ~$100M / 20%). Institutionally backed by Venture Catalysts (VCats group's 4th fund). Portfolio: smallcase, IDfy, AstroTalk (INR 110 Cr), Snapmint; exits incl. BluSmart, ReshaMandi.
investors.writeup: Elev8 Venture Partners is a Bengaluru-based, growth-stage venture firm founded in 2022 and led by co-founder and Managing Director Navin Honagudi, who previously spent over a decade as a partner at Kae Capital, where he invested in 50-plus companies including Paytm, Shiprocket and Vedantu. Elev8 runs a $200 million India-focused, sector-agnostic fund (with a debut close around $160 million), licensed as a SEBI Category-II AIF with a green-shoe option, and concentrates on Series B and C rounds in profitable, technology-driven companies that have established product-market fit and are scaling — whether for overseas expansion, inorganic acquisitions, technology-team and CXO hiring, or positioning for an eventual IPO. Ticket sizes run $5–15 million across a focused portfolio of roughly 12–14 companies, spanning consumer internet, SaaS, B2B platforms and fintech, and the firm describes itself as India's first 'Pro Rata' fund, accessing oversubscribed rounds alongside top-tier growth investors via proprietary data-driven algorithms. Elev8 is anchored by South Korea's KB Investment (part of KB Group), which committed around $100 million and supports Southeast Asia expansion, and is institutionally backed by early-stage platform Venture Catalysts. Its portfolio includes smallcase, identity-verification firm IDfy, spiritual-tech platform AstroTalk and no-credit-card EMI provider Snapmint, with the broader team's track record including exits such as BluSmart and ReshaMandi.

investors.name: India Accelerator
