investors.thesis: 'Destination Accelerator' — a fund-led, multi-stage accelerator helping startups at every stage through a rigorous, methodical cohort program across eight industry-specialised verticals, leveraging local industry, academia, legal/compliance and resource support to drive growth and impact.
investors.notes: Gurugram. Founded 2017. India's leading fund-led accelerator; first Indian member of the Global Accelerator Network (GAN); Best Accelerator 2021 (Startup India awards). Runs own SEBI Cat-I & Cat-II funds + a GIFT City fund; later-stage investing via Finvolve. 98–120+ startups; combined onboarded valuation $253M+; 12 partial exits; 5,600+ jobs created. Programs incl. Sanjeevan Healthcare (with i-Hub Gujarat) and TomorrowLAB (Tata Steel + IIT Bhubaneswar).
investors.writeup: India Accelerator (IA) is a Gurugram-based, fund-led, multi-stage startup accelerator — among the most active in the country and the first Indian program to be affiliated with the Global Accelerator Network (GAN), recognised as Best Accelerator 2021 at the Startup India awards. Built around a thesis it calls 'Destination Accelerator', IA runs a rigorous, methodical cohort program that is sector-agnostic but organised into eight industry-specialised verticals, each led by subject-matter experts and an investment committee that reviews, mentors and connects startups for growth. A key differentiator is that IA backs its cohorts with its own capital: it operates SEBI Category-I and Category-II funds and a GIFT City fund, and invests in comparatively later-stage businesses through its arm Finvolve, creating an ecosystem (its 'multiverse') designed to support companies at every stage with mentorship, market access, legal/compliance help and follow-on funding. Over recent years IA has supported more than 98–120 startups, with onboarded companies carrying a combined valuation exceeding $253 million, 12 partial exits and over 5,600 jobs created. It also runs targeted programs in partnership with institutions and corporates — including the Sanjeevan Healthcare Accelerator with i-Hub Gujarat and TomorrowLAB with Tata Steel and IIT Bhubaneswar — and unveiled a Cohort '25 offering up to $10 million in funding support.

investors.name: Enlighten Angel Fund
investors.companyTypeRaw: Angel Fund → Micro VC (SEBI AIF) [rebranded 'Enlighten Capital', Dec 2024]
investors.thesis: Support early-stage founders building disruptive solutions in emerging technologies aligned with India's innovation and sustainable-development vision; a structured investment approach backed by a strong network of LPs and angels, aimed at addressing the critical early-stage funding gap.
investors.chequeSize: Micro-VC early-stage cheques (Fund 1 INR 100 Cr + INR 100 Cr greenshoe = INR 200 Cr)
investors.notes: Chennai. Founded 2022 as Enlighten Angel Fund (EnlightenVC.online). Rebranded to Enlighten Capital (full-fledged Micro VC) in Dec 2024 after receiving SEBI AIF approval. Maiden fund: INR 100 Cr raised from LPs + INR 100 Cr greenshoe (INR 200 Cr target). GPs Koushik Shekar (ex-Sutherland, Citi) & Arvind Subramaniam; partners Goutham Sekhar, Snehali Mansingh Khamkar, Rohit Mohan; team ~7. Syndicated 10+ investments as an angel fund. Runs the iZentral startup carnival (with Startup India, i-Hub Gujarat).
investors.writeup: Enlighten Angel Fund — now rebranded as Enlighten Capital — is a Chennai-based early-stage investor founded in 2022 that, over its first two years, operated as an angel fund and syndicated more than ten investments while building a reputation for identifying and nurturing high-potential ventures. In early December 2024 it received SEBI approval to operate as an Alternative Investment Fund and rebranded into a full-fledged micro-VC, completing a ₹100 crore maiden fund (Fund 1) raised from limited partners and launching fundraising for an additional ₹100 crore greenshoe option, taking its target corpus to ₹200 crore. The fund focuses on early-stage, disruptive startups in sectors it sees as driving change — emerging technologies, smart manufacturing, mobility and fintech — explicitly aligning its thesis with India's vision for innovation and sustainable development. Enlighten is led by General Partners Koushik Shekar, who moved from technology roles at Sutherland and Citi into consulting and angel investing, and Arvind Subramaniam, an entrepreneur and operator, supported by a partner team of Goutham Sekhar, Snehali Mansingh Khamkar and Rohit Mohan. Backed by a structured investment approach and a strong network of LPs and angels, the fund positions itself as an institutional enabler addressing the critical early-stage funding gap, and runs ecosystem initiatives such as its iZentral startup carnival.

investors.name: We Founder Circle
investors.thesis: Founders-first, community-based investment platform connecting founders, angels, operators and global funds; give early-stage entrepreneurs funding visibility plus active mentoring and business support, with strong reach into Tier 2/3/4 cities and women founders. Backs founders on knowledge, experience, passion and attitude.
investors.notes: Founded Aug 2020 (Surat/Delhi). 13,000+ angel community across 80+ countries. Co-founders: Neeraj Tyagi (CEO; passed away Aug 18, 2025), Gaurav VK Singhvi, Bhawna Bhatnagar, Vikas Aggarwal, Deo Saurabh; team ~24–63 incl ~8 partners. Vehicles: EvolveX accelerator, Invstt.com platform, Avinya Ventures (VC fund), Invstt Trust (SEBI angel fund) + GIFT City fund. 134–162 startups, 200+ deals; 1 IPO (TradeUNO), 1 acquisition (Flatheads); 10x exit in OLL. 33% Tier 2/3, ~27% female founders. Portfolio: Pandorum, Zypp Electric, Stage OTT, ScrapUncle, Oben Electric, Anveshan, Garuda Aerospace.
investors.writeup: We Founder Circle (WFC) is a founders-led, community-based startup investment platform established in August 2020 that has grown into one of India's largest angel networks, with a community of more than 13,000 angels spanning over 80 countries. Built on a founders-first thesis — evaluating ventures on knowledge, experience, passion and attitude — WFC gives early-stage entrepreneurs both funding visibility and active mentoring, with a notable focus on Tier 2/3/4 cities (around a third of its portfolio) and women founders (close to 30%). The platform operates a full stack of vehicles: the EvolveX global accelerator, which provides pre-seed startups roughly $20–30K and helps them raise up to $100,000; the Invstt.com community and marketplace platform; a dedicated VC fund, Avinya Ventures; and regulated structures including a SEBI angel fund (Invstt Trust) and a GIFT City fund for global investors. Across these, WFC typically backs companies from seed to Series B with $300K–$1M cheques, sector-agnostically across EV, D2C, SaaS, robotics, fintech, agritech and more. It has invested in over 130 startups through 200-plus deals, producing an IPO (TradeUNO), an acquisition (Flatheads) and a 10x exit, with portfolio names including Zypp Electric, Oben Electric, Stage OTT, ScrapUncle, Anveshan and Garuda Aerospace. Co-founder and CEO Neeraj Tyagi, who led the firm, passed away in August 2025.

investors.name: Kathyawad Ventures
investors.thesis: Empower startups with connections, expertise and hands-on support — notably through its 'Scaleation' / 3rd Horizon Scaleators program — to help them navigate scaling challenges and build sustainable, steadily-growing companies.
investors.notes: Ahmedabad. Founded 2022. Small team of ~8 (1 partner + 7 venture partners; India & Romania). Runs the '3rd Horizon Scaleators' / Scaleation program for growth-stage startups. Few disclosed investments: agprop (led seed, 2023), SR Charging Stations (EV charging), Varistor Technologies. Limited public data on fund size and cheque size.
investors.writeup: Kathyawad Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm based in Ahmedabad, founded in 2022, that focuses on seed-stage investments in Indian startups while emphasising hands-on scaling support. A distinctive feature is its 'Scaleation' / 3rd Horizon Scaleators program — a structured 'scaleator' designed specifically for growth-stage startups navigating the difficult journey from problem identification and ideation through market entry and scale, where the firm provides connections, domain expertise and operational guidance. Backed by what it describes as a decade of financial expertise, Kathyawad concentrates on sectors including enterprise SaaS, software infrastructure, consumer services, fintech, healthcare, the future of work, and real estate and construction tech, with a stated emphasis on building sustainable companies. Its team of around eight spans a partner and several venture partners across India and Romania. Public disclosure on the firm is limited — its fund size and typical cheque size are not published, and only a handful of investments are on record, including agtech/proptech startup agprop (a seed round it led in 2023), EV-charging network SR Charging Stations and clean-energy/fire-safety firm Varistor Technologies — so this profile is intentionally conservative pending further confirmation.

investors.name: 100Unicorns
investors.companyTypeRaw: Accelerator VC fund (idea/early-stage; flagship fund of Venture Catalysts Group)
investors.thesis: Be the 'Y Combinator of India' — provide initial capital plus committed follow-on to idea-stage startups, supporting them across their first three funding rounds before connecting them to large VCs for growth capital.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2020 as 9Unicorns; rebranded to 100Unicorns in 2024. Flagship accelerator-VC fund of Venture Catalysts Group. Co-founders Apoorva Ranjan Sharma (MD), Gaurav Jain, Anil Jain, Anuj Golecha. Fund I $100M (140–185 startups, ~9 exits); Fund II $200M + $100M green-shoe (target 200 startups), with UAE/ADGM presence; ~15% allocated to US/MENA/Africa/Asia. Portfolio: VideoVerse, Zypp Electric, Renee Cosmetics, Trunativ, IGP, LiquiLoans, ImpactGuru.
investors.writeup: 100Unicorns — formerly 9Unicorns — is a Mumbai-based accelerator venture capital fund founded in 2020 as the flagship early-stage vehicle of the Venture Catalysts Group, and is often described as India's first accelerator VC. Co-founded by Apoorva Ranjan Sharma (also Managing Director of Venture Catalysts) along with Gaurav Jain, Anil Jain and Anuj Golecha, its explicit ambition is to become 'the Y Combinator of India', backing promising founders right from the ideation stage with initial capital plus committed follow-on, and supporting them across their first three funding rounds before connecting them to larger VCs for growth capital. Its first fund closed at $100 million and invested in more than 140 startups across fintech, deeptech, enterprise SaaS, media, insurtech and D2C, producing several category leaders and around nine exits. In 2024 the firm rebranded to 100Unicorns and launched a second fund targeting $200 million with a $100 million green-shoe, aiming to back 200 early-stage startups; roughly 60% of the corpus funds first cheques of $250K–$300K with follow-ons up to $3 million, and about 15% is earmarked for startups in the US, Middle East, Africa and Asia, supported by a new ADGM presence in the UAE. Portfolio names include VideoVerse, Zypp Electric, Renee Cosmetics, Trunativ, IGP, LiquiLoans and ImpactGuru.

investors.name: Next Star Venture Capital LLP
investors.thesis: Operate as a Corporate Venture Capital arm that backs and builds acquisitions to disrupt industries and improve lives — dedicating resources and specialised teams to 'architect the NEXT Stars'; occasionally co-invests with like-minded investors.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2018. Small team of ~3 (2 partners + 1 principal). Operates as a Corporate Venture Capital (CVC); grew out of a founder group that built datacenter and software-services companies with 2,000+ employees. Limited public disclosure on fund size, cheque size and portfolio. (Distinct from Sorin Investment Mgmt, Next Orbit Ventures and Nu Ventures, which are unrelated.)
investors.writeup: Next Star Venture Capital LLP is a Mumbai-based investment firm founded in 2018 that operates primarily as a Corporate Venture Capital (CVC) vehicle. According to the firm, its journey began as a startup that created companies spanning datacenters and software services, growing to over 2,000 employees, and it now channels that operating experience into venture investing — backing and building acquisitions that aim to disrupt industries and improve lives, while dedicating teams and resources to 'architect the NEXT Stars'. It occasionally invites like-minded co-investors into its deals. The firm is small and sector-agnostic, run by a compact team of around three (two partners and a principal). Public disclosure is very limited: its fund size, typical cheque size and a named portfolio are not publicly available, and it should not be confused with similarly named but unrelated firms such as Sorin Investment Management, Next Orbit Ventures or Nu Ventures. This profile is therefore intentionally conservative and would benefit from primary confirmation of strategy and track record.

investors.name: Artha Venture Fund
investors.companyTypeRaw: Micro-VC (early-stage; multi-stage platform via Artha India Ventures family office)
investors.thesis: Pioneer of India's micro-VC model — back tech-enabled (not tech-first) 'category creators' from day zero, combining early-stage experience, operator insight, family-office networks and institutional discipline; concentrate capital on winners via a proprietary '1–2–4' escalating follow-on model.
investors.notes: Mumbai. India's first early-stage micro-VC. MP Anirudh A. Damani (2nd-gen investor, 4th-gen entrepreneur). Backed by Artha India Ventures (family office of Ashok Kumar & Ramesh Damani) + Singularity Ventures (Madhusudan Kela). AVF I INR 225 Cr (final close 2021), 32 seed startups, 61% IRR; Artha Select Fund (winners-only) final close INR 432 Cr/$49.4M (2025); AVF II INR 500 Cr target (INR 250 Cr first close Oct 2025) + INR 100 Cr green-shoe, 36 seed startups. Platform AUM ~INR 2,100–2,300 Cr; 130–140 cos since 2012. Portfolio: OYO, Rapido, Purplle, Everest Fleet, Agnikul Cosmos, InstaAstro.
investors.writeup: Artha Venture Fund (AVF) is a Mumbai-based, early-stage micro-VC widely regarded as a pioneer of India's micro-venture model, led by Managing Partner Anirudh A. Damani — a second-generation investor and fourth-generation entrepreneur — and backed by Artha India Ventures, the family office of Ashok Kumar and Ramesh Damani, alongside Madhusudan Kela's Singularity Ventures. Artha backs tech-enabled (deliberately not 'tech-first') category creators from day zero, combining operator insight, family-office networks and institutional discipline, and concentrates capital on winners through a proprietary '1–2–4' escalating follow-on model. Its debut fund (AVF I), a roughly ₹225 crore Category-I AIF closed in 2021, deployed across 32 seed-stage startups and has reported a 61% IRR with portfolio valuation exceeding ₹750 crore and FY25 portfolio revenues over ₹2,100 crore. A 'winners-only' follow-on vehicle, the Artha Select Fund, closed at about ₹432 crore ($49 million) in 2025 to back the top 15% of its portfolio in Series B/C rounds. In October 2025 Artha announced the first close (₹250 crore) of Artha Venture Fund II, targeting ₹500 crore plus a ₹100 crore green-shoe to back 36 seed-stage startups across premium consumption, fintech infrastructure, applied AI and deeptech, with ₹4 crore initial cheques. Across its platform — managing roughly ₹2,100–2,300 crore — Artha has backed 130-plus companies including OYO, Rapido, Purplle, Everest Fleet and Agnikul Cosmos.

investors.name: Aarin Capital
investors.companyTypeRaw: Proprietary Venture Fund + Fund-of-Funds / Family Office (multi-asset)
investors.thesis: Build an expansive, India-centric platform of investment opportunities — make direct investments in technology-driven businesses with large India-first market potential, while seeding and anchoring entrepreneurial fund managers as a prime LP to broaden access to the startup ecosystem and keep companies domiciled in India.
investors.notes: Bengaluru. Founded ~2011 by T.V. Mohandas Pai (ex-Infosys CFO/board) & Dr. Ranjan Pai (Manipal Education & Medical Group) — the two are not related. MD Deepak Natraj. ~$150M proprietary fund + Fund-of-Funds; seeded/anchored 10+ funds (3one4 Capital, Exfinity Venture Partners, Ideaspring, Saha Fund) as prime LP. ~$450M ecosystem, 266 investments, 35 independent fund managers. Portfolio/exits: Byju's, PharmEasy (API Holdings), HomeLane, ZoomCar, Licious, Kapiva, Faircent, 88academics.
investors.writeup: Aarin Capital is a Bengaluru-based proprietary venture fund and fund-of-funds, co-founded around 2011 by T.V. Mohandas Pai — the former CFO and board member of Infosys and a Padma Shri awardee — and Dr. Ranjan Pai, chairman of the Manipal Education and Medical Group (the two share a surname but are not related). Structured partly as a family office spanning multiple asset classes, Aarin makes direct investments in startups while also acting as a prime limited partner across 10-to-15-plus funds covering early- and growth-stage venture capital, public markets, real estate project financing, hedge funds and private equity. Its direct thesis centres on technology-driven businesses in life sciences, healthcare and education with large, India-centric or India-first market opportunities, and it has progressively expanded into impact areas such as climate tech and agritech. A distinctive feature is its role as an ecosystem builder: Aarin has helped launch and seed funds including 3one4 Capital, Exfinity Venture Partners, Ideaspring Capital and Saha Fund, where the Pais serve as both GPs and LPs, supported by around 35 independent fund managers across a roughly $450 million ecosystem. Its direct portfolio and exits include Byju's, PharmEasy, HomeLane, ZoomCar, Licious, Kapiva and Faircent. The firm explicitly works to keep promising Indian companies domiciled in India.

investors.name: Catamaran
investors.companyTypeRaw: Global Investment Firm / Family Office (multi-asset: public equity, PE, growth VC)
investors.thesis: Be a globally-respected catalyst that converts the ideas of passionate, skilled, value-driven entrepreneurs into tangible business outcomes; a long-term investor that prizes relationships, corporate governance and sustainable value creation across stages.
investors.notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2009 by N.R. Narayana Murthy (Infosys founder); manages the assets of the Murthy family. >$1B AUM across public equity, PE and growth VC. President Deepak Padaki; Chairman MD Ranganath (ex-Infosys CFO). Original Catamaran Venture Fund ~INR 600 Cr; first deal SKS Microfinance (2010). ~37 investments, 3 exits. Portfolio: SpaceX, udaan, Udemy, Acko, Log 9, Manipal Health. Distinct from Catamaran Ventures UK (Akshata Murty's, winding down).
investors.writeup: Catamaran is a Bengaluru-based global investment firm and family office established in 2009 by N.R. Narayana Murthy, the founder of Infosys, to manage the assets of Murthy and his family. Managing over $1 billion across asset classes — spanning public equity, private equity and growth-stage venture capital — Catamaran describes its purpose as being a catalyst that converts the ideas of passionate, skilled and value-driven entrepreneurs into tangible business outcomes, and it positions itself as a patient, long-term investor that prizes relationships, corporate governance and sustainable value creation. Its original venture vehicle, the roughly ₹600 crore Catamaran Venture Fund, made its first investment in SKS Microfinance and initially targeted healthcare, education and nutrition; over time the platform has built a diverse portfolio that includes SpaceX, deep-tech energy startup Log 9, B2B e-commerce leader udaan, edtech firm Udemy and fintech player Acko, among around 37 investments. Led by President Deepak Padaki and Chairman M.D. Ranganath (a former Infosys CFO), Catamaran has more recently signalled a focus on services and precision manufacturing — backing startups capable of exporting deep-tech and automotive components as India attracts manufacturing investment. It is a separate entity from the now-winding-down UK-based Catamaran Ventures associated with Akshata Murty, with no investment overlap between the two.

investors.name: Pratithi Investments
investors.companyTypeRaw: Single Family Office (Kris Gopalakrishnan family) — SEBI Cat-II AIF + FoF
investors.thesis: Support entrepreneurship, technological advances and scientific research in India; back growth/late-stage startups with great founders, strong products and high standards of corporate governance, co-investing alongside leading institutional investors with a similar long-term approach.
investors.chequeSize: Late-stage debt & equity (family-office cheques); also LP commitments to funds
investors.notes: Bengaluru. Founded 2014/2015. Single family office / private investment arm of Kris Gopalakrishnan (Infosys co-founder; Padma Bhushan; chairman of Axilor Ventures). Managed via Prayog Advisors LLP; runs the Pratithi Investment Fund (SEBI Cat-II AIF). 100+ startups (81 India, 6 US), 7 unicorns (Yubi, Uniphore, XpressBees). Recent deals: Planys Technologies, Agnikul, JetSynthesys. Related family entities: Pratiksha Trust (R&D/innovation philanthropy with IISc, IIT Madras), SGK Trust (real estate).
investors.writeup: Pratithi Investments is the single family office and private investment arm of the Kris Gopalakrishnan family, founded around 2014-15 and based in Bengaluru. Kris Gopalakrishnan is a co-founder of Infosys, a Padma Bhushan awardee and chairman of the Axilor Ventures accelerator, and Pratithi reflects his conviction that the nation's growth will be fuelled by the innovation and enterprise of its people. Administered through Prayog Advisors LLP and investing via the SEBI Category-II Pratithi Investment Fund, the firm's mission is to support entrepreneurship, technological advances and scientific research in India. It is sector-agnostic and primarily backs growth and late-stage startups — across both debt and equity — while also committing as a limited partner to venture capital, private equity and debt funds across stages. Its investment approach centres on the quality of the founding team, the scale of the opportunity and a high standard of corporate governance, and it typically co-invests alongside leading institutional investors. Since launching, Pratithi has backed over a hundred startups across sectors, including seven unicorns such as Yubi, Uniphore and XpressBees, with recent participation in deep-tech and space names like Planys Technologies and Agnikul. The broader family platform also encompasses the Pratiksha Trust, which funds R&D and innovation in brain science and computing at institutions such as IISc and IIT Madras.

investors.name: Spectrum Impact
investors.companyTypeRaw: Single Family Office (impact; Gogri family / Aarti Industries) — for-profit + not-for-profit pools
investors.thesis: Solve large-scale societal problems with novel solutions; allocate for-profit and not-for-profit pools of capital to optimise financial, societal and environmental returns — backing technologies and businesses that aim to arrest and reverse climate change, alongside organisations making health and education more accessible and affordable.
investors.notes: Mumbai. Founded 2021. Single family office of Rajendra & Arti Gogri (promoters of Aarti Industries Ltd, specialty chemicals). Two capital pools (for-profit + not-for-profit). 51 portfolio cos (~5 new/yr); team 6 incl 2 partners; 1 acquisition. Portfolio: Atomberg, Miko Technologies, Cityflo, Blue Sky Analytics, EEKI Foods, Ashaya, Polycycl, Kreedo, Volt14, MOOEV. Co-invests with Blume, Omnivore, Inflection Point Ventures. (Distinct from the US impact-investing consultancy 'Spectrum Impact' run by Rehana Nathoo.)
investors.writeup: Spectrum Impact is a Mumbai-based single family office founded in 2021 to manage the assets and investments of Rajendra and Arti Gogri, promoters of Aarti Industries Limited, a leading Indian specialty-chemicals company. The firm is committed to solving large-scale societal problems with novel solutions, and operates two distinct pools of capital — a proprietary for-profit pool and a separate not-for-profit pool — allocating across both to optimise financial, societal and environmental returns simultaneously. Its core focus is backing technologies and businesses that aim to arrest and reverse climate change, alongside organisations working to make health and education more accessible and affordable. Reflecting this, its portfolio spans climate tech, deep tech, clean energy, sustainable agriculture, alternate materials, health and education. Spectrum invests primarily at the seed and early stage and has built a portfolio of around 51 companies, supported by a small team of about six including two partners. Notable investments include energy-efficient-appliance maker Atomberg, robotics firm Miko Technologies, urban-mobility company Cityflo, geospatial-data startup Blue Sky Analytics, hydroponics venture EEKI Foods, waste-innovation enterprise Ashaya, plastic-recycling firm Polycycl and battery-tech startup Volt14, frequently co-investing with funds such as Blume Ventures, Omnivore and Inflection Point Ventures. It should not be confused with the unrelated US impact-investing consultancy of the same name.

investors.name: Reddy Ventures
investors.companyTypeRaw: Single Family Office (GVK / G V Sanjay Reddy family) — investment, growth & philanthropic platform
investors.thesis: Back far-sighted entrepreneurial teams and take strategic equity positions in category-defining tech companies, while incubating its own businesses; invest across 'private exponentials (technology), public compounders (equities) and fundamentals'; bring new technologies to India and take transformative Indian innovations to the world. Purpose: 'Enabling Ideas that change the world.'
investors.chequeSize: Co-invests alongside leading global angels & VCs (family-office cheques)
investors.notes: Hyderabad. Founded 2015 (formerly Keshav Reddy Family Office); the investment/growth/philanthropic platform of the G V Sanjay Reddy family (GVK Group). Runs the Reddy Futures Fund — a pure-play fund co-investing with top global angels/VCs. Led by GV Sanjay Reddy & Pinky Reddy; Keshav Reddy (MBA MIT, BSE Michigan; ex-VP GVK Airports; founder of Equal) runs the fund. ~22–30 investments, 5–6 unicorns: CRED, Upstox, Khatabook, Chipper Cash, Hive (Hive AI), Genies. Philanthropy: Pinky & Sanjay Reddy Foundation (education/healthcare); GVK EMRI (world's largest free ambulance service — 15,000 ambulances).
investors.writeup: Reddy Ventures is the investment, growth and philanthropic platform of the G V Sanjay Reddy family — part of the GVK Group — headquartered in Hyderabad and founded in 2015 (formerly the Keshav Reddy Family Office). The family began treating startups as a distinct asset class through its Reddy Futures Fund, a 'pure-play' vehicle that invests alongside some of the best angel investors and VCs globally in technology startups, complementing the family's existing allocations to real estate, public equities, bonds and group companies. The fund is run by Keshav Reddy — an MIT MBA and former Vice President at GVK Airports, founder of digital-identity startup Equal, and a board member of Aragen Life Sciences and GVK EMRI — while GV Sanjay Reddy and Pinky Reddy lead the broader platform. As active, hands-on partners, Reddy Ventures takes meaningful stakes and offers mentorship and resources across sectors such as fintech, commerce, edtech, community and lifestyle, and design. Its portfolio of roughly 30 investments includes five to six unicorns — CRED, Upstox, Khatabook, Chipper Cash, Hive (Hive AI) and Genies. The family is also deeply philanthropic: Pinky Reddy leads foundation work in education and healthcare, and the family-owned GVK EMRI operates the world's largest free ambulance service, with a fleet of around 15,000 ambulances serving hundreds of millions across India.

investors.name: 2am VC
investors.thesis: A sector-agnostic, Gen Z-centric, 'India Only' early-stage fund backing young and first-time Indian founders building uniquely Indian companies for the 'New India' opportunity; acts as a hyperlocal bridge connecting global investors with Indian founders, prioritising speed, transparency and founder-friendliness, and leads over half of its deals.
investors.chequeSize: Pre-seed/seed (Fund II: 60% initial / 40% follow-on); invests via iSAFE, SAFE, convertible notes & priced rounds
investors.notes: Offices in Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Los Angeles. Founded 2021 by Founding Partners Hershel Mehta & Brendan Rogers (co-founder of Wag!, NASDAQ: PET). Fund I $10M, ~47–48 startups; Fund II (2025) targets up to 30 startups, pre-seed to seed. 54–59 portfolio cos, 1 unicorn (Zepto), 3 acquisitions (Krave Mart, Coolberg). Portfolio: NEWME, Apna Mart, Bimaplan, Karbon Card, Blitzllama, Procureyard, inframandi, Fibr, Intervue. Co-invests with Titan Capital, 3one4, Y Combinator, Orios, India Quotient, 100X.VC.
investors.writeup: 2am VC is an early-stage, India-focused venture firm founded in 2021 by Founding Partners Hershel Mehta and Brendan Rogers (the latter also a co-founder of Nasdaq-listed Wag!), with offices across Mumbai, Bengaluru, Delhi NCR and Los Angeles. The firm describes itself as a sector-agnostic, Gen Z-centric, 'India Only' fund, built on the conviction that the next stage of India's startup development will be driven by young and first-time founders building uniquely Indian companies — what it calls the 'New India' opportunity. Blending Indian and international perspectives, 2am VC positions itself as a hyperlocal partner that bridges global investors and Indian founders, emphasising speed, transparency, founder-friendliness and cross-border synergies, and it aims to lead more than half of its deals, investing via iSAFE, SAFE, convertible notes and priced rounds. Its $10 million debut fund backed around 47 companies; in 2025 it launched Fund II to invest in up to 30 startups predominantly at pre-seed to seed across consumer tech, fintech, food and beverage, AI and global SaaS, reserving 60% for initial cheques and 40% for follow-ons. Across roughly 54–59 portfolio companies — including NEWME, Apna Mart, Bimaplan, Karbon Card, Fibr and Intervue — it counts one unicorn (Zepto) and three acquisitions.

investors.name: WestBridge Capital
investors.companyTypeRaw: Investment firm (growth/PE + public equities; evergreen, India-focused)
investors.thesis: Partner for the long term with some of India's most promising mid-sized companies — public or private — run by outstanding entrepreneurs and management teams; provide patient, purpose-driven capital via an evergreen structure, taking substantial (often minority) stakes, frequently second only to the founder, and holding for years or decades while helping companies succeed.
investors.notes: India-focused, public + private markets; based across India and Silicon Valley. Founded 2000 (one of India's first VC funds); merged with Sequoia Capital to form Sequoia Capital India (2006); revived as an independent firm in 2011 when founders Sumir Chadha, KP Balaraj, Sandeep Singhal & SK Jain left Sequoia India. Evergreen fund; AUM crossed $7–10B+; raised a $1.5B crossover fund (2023). 132 companies (104 India startups), 8 unicorns, 19 soonicorns. Portfolio: PhysicsWallah, LeadSquared, Vedantu, LEAD, Star Health, India Shelter, Aptus, Rapido, Innovaccer; listed Axis Bank, Dr Lal PathLabs, Havells, Mindtree, IndiGo.
investors.writeup: WestBridge Capital is an India-focused investment firm that invests across both public and private markets, with teams in India and Silicon Valley. Originally founded in 2000 as one of India's pioneering venture funds, it merged with Sequoia Capital in 2006 to form Sequoia Capital India; then in 2011 its founding managing directors — Sumir Chadha, K.P. Balaraj, Sandeep Singhal and S.K. Jain — separated the India-focused funds from Sequoia to re-establish WestBridge as an independent firm. WestBridge runs an evergreen, long-term, patient-capital model with assets under management that have crossed roughly $7–10 billion, and in 2023 it raised a $1.5 billion crossover fund, its largest-ever commitment for Indian companies. Its strategy is to partner with promising mid-sized businesses run by outstanding entrepreneurs — whether public or private — typically writing cheques of $25 million to $200 million for substantial, often minority, stakes (frequently second only to the founder) and holding for years or decades while taking board seats and providing operational support. Spanning Series A to IPO and beyond, its portfolio of around 132 companies includes eight unicorns such as PhysicsWallah, LeadSquared and Vedantu, plus listed names like Axis Bank, Dr Lal PathLabs, Havells, Mindtree and IndiGo, and newer bets including Star Health, India Shelter, Rapido and Innovaccer.

investors.name: Aarii Ventures
investors.thesis: Back ambitious founders building technology-driven businesses
investors.notes: Early-stage India-focused micro VC
investors.writeup: Aarii Ventures is an India-focused micro VC that backs ambitious founders at the earliest stages of company building. The firm is active at pre-seed and seed, writing cheques between $100k and $500k, positioning it as a meaningful first or co-lead institutional partner for founders who are just beginning to raise external capital. Aarii's sector interest spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C, reflecting a broad appetite for technology-driven business models with scalable unit economics. The firm's thesis centers on backing founders with strong conviction and a clear product vision, rather than requiring extensive traction at the point of investment. For Indian founders navigating the earliest and often most difficult stage of fundraising, Aarii Ventures represents the kind of early believer that can anchor a round and provide foundational credibility with later-stage investors. Founders building in the firm's focus sectors who are raising their first institutional round should consider Aarii as a relevant target, particularly if they are working on India-first problems with potential to scale. Reaching out through LinkedIn or the firm's website is the recommended approach for initial introductions.

investors.name: Midas Capital | Baheti Family Office
investors.thesis: Invest in founders building scalable, tech-enabled businesses
investors.notes: Baheti family office; Jaipur-based
investors.writeup: Midas Capital is the investment arm of the Baheti family office, headquartered in Jaipur. The firm invests at Seed and Pre-Series A stages with cheque sizes ranging from $250k to $2M, making it a meaningful early institutional backer for Indian founders. Their focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C sectors, with a preference for businesses that leverage technology to build scalable, defensible models. Being a family office, Midas Capital typically offers founders a faster, more relationship-driven decision-making process compared to institutional VC funds, with flexibility on deal structuring. Founders can expect engagement from principals who have a long-term capital orientation and skin in the game beyond a fund cycle. Their Jaipur base also means they carry a practical, grounded perspective on India's non-metro consumer and business landscape, which can be an asset for founders targeting Bharat-centric markets. If you are raising your first or second institutional round and are building in their core sectors, Midas Capital is worth approaching with a crisp deck and early traction metrics.

investors.name: Midas Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in founders building scalable, tech-enabled businesses
investors.notes: Baheti family office managing VC investments
investors.writeup: Midas Capital is the venture investment arm of the Baheti family office, focused on early-stage startups in India. Operating at Seed and Pre-Series A, they write cheques between $250k and $2M, making them a meaningful lead or co-lead option for founders raising their first institutional round or a bridge into a larger Series A. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C, reflecting an interest in technology-driven businesses that can demonstrate capital efficiency and scalable unit economics. As a family office, Midas Capital typically brings a longer investment horizon and a less rigid return timeline than traditional institutional funds, which can translate into more founder-friendly terms and patient capital during the early scaling phase. Founders pitching Midas should be prepared to articulate a clear path to scale, strong technology differentiation, and a defensible market position. Given the family office structure, decision-making can be faster and more direct than multi-partner VC funds. Founders in B2B SaaS, consumer tech, or fintech infrastructure who are at the point of proving initial traction and looking for a conviction-driven early backer would be well-suited to engage with this firm.

investors.name: Unilazer Ventures
investors.thesis: Back growth-oriented entrepreneurs building differentiated businesses
investors.notes: Ronnie Screwvala's investment fund; backed Upgrad, Ustraa
investors.writeup: Unilazer Ventures is the investment vehicle of Ronnie Screwvala, one of India's most respected entrepreneurs and the founder of UTV Group. The firm invests at Seed and Series A stages, with cheque sizes typically ranging from $500k to $5M, focusing on Consumer, D2C, FinTech, and HealthTech. What sets Unilazer apart is the value Ronnie personally brings beyond capital — deep brand-building instincts, a vast network across media, entertainment, and corporate India, and a genuine empathy for the founder journey having built and scaled businesses himself. Portfolio companies like upGrad and Ustraa reflect the firm's appetite for category-defining consumer businesses with strong brand DNA. Founders pitching to Unilazer should expect an engaged, hands-on relationship rather than a passive investor dynamic. The firm favors entrepreneurs who are building differentiated businesses with a clear path to scale, and who are not just chasing trends but are genuinely solving meaningful consumer needs. If you are an early-stage founder in a consumer-facing or digitally-enabled sector looking for a strategic partner with real operational credibility, Unilazer Ventures is worth a direct, well-prepared approach.

investors.name: Hunch Ventures & Investments Pvt Ltd
investors.thesis: Back founders who have a strong vision and ability to execute
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Hunch Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the earliest and often most formative stages of their journey, from Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A. The firm's investment approach is firmly founder-first: the team looks for individuals who combine a compelling, differentiated vision with a demonstrated ability to execute against it, which is a combination that is especially critical in the competitive Indian startup landscape. Hunch Ventures invests across four core sectors, SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, and D2C, reflecting a belief that India's domestic demand story and digital infrastructure create durable tailwinds in each of these categories. Cheque sizes range from $100,000 to $1 million, making the firm a natural fit for founders who are raising their first institutional round or bridging toward a larger Series A. Founders approaching Hunch Ventures should be prepared to articulate not just a market opportunity but a clear-eyed plan for how they intend to build and scale their business. The firm's positioning at the earliest stages means it is comfortable with uncertainty but expects founders to bring conviction, domain insight, and a credible path forward.

investors.name: Aroa Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Partner with early-stage founders leveraging technology for scale
investors.notes: India-focused early stage micro VC
investors.writeup: Aroa Venture Partners is an India-focused micro VC operating at the pre-seed and seed stages, making it one of the earlier institutional checks a founder can receive. The firm writes cheques between $100,000 and $500,000, a range that suits founders who have a working hypothesis and early traction but are not yet ready for a large Series A institutional round. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B, reflecting a broad interest in technology-enabled business models that can scale efficiently across Indian and global markets. The core philosophy is to partner with founders early, when the risk is highest but so is the potential to shape the company's direction meaningfully. For founders, this means Aroa is likely to be engaged beyond the cheque, offering support through the earliest and often most uncertain phases of company building. If you are a founder building in any of these sectors and are raising your first or second institutional round, Aroa Venture Partners is worth reaching out to early in your fundraising process before your round fills up.

investors.name: Aakash Emprise Pvt Ltd
investors.thesis: Invest in high-quality teams solving large market problems
investors.notes: Family office with active VC investing
investors.writeup: Aakash Emprise Pvt Ltd is an Indian family office that actively participates in early-stage venture investing, bridging the conviction-driven mindset of a family office with the hands-on engagement of a VC. The firm focuses on Seed and Pre-Series A rounds, deploying cheques in the $250k to $2M range, which positions it well to lead or co-lead early rounds for Indian startups. Their sector interest spans SaaS, FinTech, and Consumer, three of the most active verticals in the Indian startup ecosystem. The core investment philosophy centers on backing high-quality teams who are going after genuinely large market problems, suggesting that team quality and market size are weighted heavily in diligence conversations. For founders, this means demonstrating founder-market fit and a credible path to scale will likely resonate more than near-term revenue metrics alone. As a family office, Aakash Emprise can offer patient capital and decision-making that is often faster and less committee-driven than institutional funds, making them a practical option for founders seeking a collaborative early partner with meaningful cheque sizes.

investors.name: Malpani Ventures
investors.thesis: Back smart founders with bold ideas at the earliest stage
investors.notes: Aniruddha Malpani's investment vehicle; angel-first approach
investors.writeup: Malpani Ventures is the investment vehicle of Dr. Aniruddha Malpani, one of India's most recognisable and outspoken angel investors. Operating at the pre-seed and seed stage, the firm backs founders before most institutional capital is willing to engage, making it a meaningful first cheque for early-stage companies. Cheque sizes typically range from $50,000 to $500,000, suitable for founders raising their first or second round. The firm has a broad sector mandate covering SaaS, FinTech, and consumer businesses, and does not restrict itself to a single vertical, which makes it accessible to a wide range of founding teams. Dr. Malpani is known in the Indian startup ecosystem for his directness, his commitment to founder education, and his willingness to engage even before a formal pitch. Founders who approach Malpani Ventures should come with a crisp articulation of the problem they are solving, a credible reason why they are the right team to solve it, and a genuine openness to feedback. The firm values intellectual honesty and long-term thinking over short-term vanity metrics. For founders at the earliest stage who want an experienced, engaged angel rather than a passive cheque, Malpani Ventures is worth a direct outreach.

investors.name: Siana Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in growth-stage technology companies in India
investors.notes: Growth-stage India-focused VC; founded by Siddharth Pai
investors.writeup: Siana Capital is a growth-stage venture capital firm focused exclusively on India's technology ecosystem. Founded by Siddharth Pai, who brings extensive experience from the technology services and advisory world, the firm is designed to back founders who have moved past early experimentation and are ready to scale with institutional capital and strategic support. Siana invests at Series A and Series B, writing cheques typically between $2M and $20M, which positions it well for companies that have validated their model and are pursuing aggressive go-to-market or product expansion. The firm's sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer tech, and B2B/Enterprise software, reflecting a broad but deliberate appetite for businesses where technology creates durable competitive advantage. For founders, Siana's differentiation lies in the operating depth and industry networks Siddharth Pai brings from years at the intersection of global technology and India-specific execution. This makes the firm particularly relevant for startups that need more than capital at the growth stage and are looking for a partner who understands the nuances of scaling technology businesses in India's complex market environment.

investors.name: Rainmatter
investors.thesis: Invest in companies improving financial wellbeing and sustainability in India
investors.notes: Zerodha's innovation fund; backed Smallcase, Streak, Ditto, GreenJams
investors.writeup: Rainmatter is the innovation fund and venture arm of Zerodha, India's largest retail brokerage by active clients. It backs early-stage startups across FinTech, CleanTech, HealthTech, and Consumer sectors, typically writing cheques between $100k and $5 million at Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A stages. What makes Rainmatter distinctly valuable for founders is the strategic advantage of being associated with the Zerodha ecosystem — access to a large, financially engaged user base, product and distribution know-how, and a network deeply embedded in Indian retail finance. The firm is thematically driven rather than return-first in its framing, gravitating toward businesses that improve the financial lives of ordinary Indians or advance sustainability. Founders in fintech infrastructure, personal finance, climate solutions, or preventive health will find a receptive audience here. Rainmatter tends to be hands-on with portfolio companies on product thinking, and its association signals credibility with subsequent investors. Founders should come prepared with a clear articulation of user impact, not just market size.

investors.name: Easy Knowledge Club
investors.thesis: Enable founders through capital and knowledge-sharing
investors.notes: Community-driven angel investment platform
investors.writeup: Easy Knowledge Club, operating as Indicorn Angels, is a community-driven angel network targeting early-stage Indian startups at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages. The platform differentiates itself by pairing capital with structured knowledge-sharing, meaning founders who come on board gain access not only to cheques in the range of $50,000 to $250,000 but also to a network of experienced angels who actively engage with portfolio companies. The network has a clear sectoral focus spanning EdTech, Consumer, SaaS, and FinTech, making it particularly relevant for founders building in these spaces within the Indian market. The community-first approach suggests that founders should come prepared to engage meaningfully with the network rather than treating this as a purely transactional relationship. For first-time or early founders who benefit from mentorship, peer learning, and warm introductions alongside funding, Indicorn Angels presents a compelling option. Founders approaching this network should highlight not only their traction and market opportunity but also how they plan to contribute to and learn from the broader angel community. The emphasis on knowledge exchange reflects a thesis that capital alone is insufficient at the earliest stages of company building.

investors.name: Fluid Ventures
investors.thesis: Flexible and founder-friendly early-stage investing
investors.notes: India early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: Fluid Ventures is an India-based micro VC firm focused on backing founders at the earliest stages of company building, typically at Pre-Seed and Seed. The firm writes cheques in the range of $100k to $500k, making it particularly relevant for founders raising their first institutional round or bridging into a larger Seed. Fluid Ventures invests across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B sectors, giving it broad exposure to the Indian startup ecosystem rather than a narrow vertical focus. What distinguishes Fluid Ventures is its stated commitment to being flexible and founder-friendly, which in practice typically means faster decision-making, less bureaucratic term sheet processes, and a willingness to work around founder-specific constraints. For early-stage Indian founders who need a nimble institutional partner rather than a large fund with lengthy diligence cycles, Fluid Ventures fits well. Founders approaching the firm should be prepared to articulate early traction, product direction, and a clear sense of the Indian or global market opportunity. Given the micro VC positioning, Fluid Ventures is likely comfortable with pre-revenue or very early revenue stages, making it a practical first call for founders just beginning to build out their cap table.

investors.name: GSF
investors.thesis: Accelerate India's tech ecosystem through capital and mentoring
investors.notes: Global Super Angels Forum; accelerator with strong network
investors.writeup: GSF, the Global Super Angels Forum, is one of India's earliest and most recognized accelerator-cum-investor platforms, built specifically to support founders at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages. It operates at the intersection of structured acceleration and angel investing, offering cohort-based programs that pair capital with deep mentorship from seasoned entrepreneurs, operators, and investors across India and globally. GSF's sweet spot lies in SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, and DeepTech startups, and its cheque sizes typically range from $50k to $250k, making it well-suited for founders seeking their first institutional backing alongside hands-on support. The platform's defining value beyond capital is its network: GSF has cultivated a community of super angels who actively engage with portfolio companies on go-to-market strategy, fundraising, and international expansion. For Indian founders at a very early stage who want more than just a wire transfer, GSF offers a community-oriented environment with genuine mentorship infrastructure. Founders should expect a collaborative, cohort-driven experience and come prepared with a clear product thesis and early traction or a compelling market insight.

investors.name: ZeCa Capital
investors.thesis: Back early-stage founders in India with capital and community
investors.notes: Community-driven micro VC
investors.writeup: ZeCa Capital is a community-driven micro VC investing in early-stage Indian startups at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages. The fund focuses on four core verticals — SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, and D2C — and writes cheques ranging from $100k to $500k, positioning itself well for founders raising their first meaningful institutional round. What sets ZeCa apart from traditional micro VCs is its emphasis on community alongside capital. The firm believes that early-stage founders benefit as much from peer networks, shared learnings, and founder support systems as they do from the cheque itself. This makes ZeCa particularly relevant for first-time or early founders who need both funding and an ecosystem to grow within. If you are building in one of their core sectors and are at an idea-to-early-traction stage, ZeCa is worth approaching. Founders should come prepared with a clear articulation of the problem they are solving, early signals of market validation, and an understanding of how they would use the community aspect of ZeCa's model to accelerate their growth. The fund's lean structure also means founders can expect relatively direct and responsive engagement compared to larger institutional players.

investors.name: seafund
investors.thesis: Back founders building scalable businesses in Southeast Asia and India
investors.notes: India/SEA focused early-stage fund
investors.writeup: SEA Fund is an early-stage venture capital firm investing across India and Southeast Asia, targeting founders at the Seed and Pre-Series A stages. The fund writes cheques in the $250K to $2M range, making it well suited for startups that have achieved early product validation and are beginning to show traction but need capital to scale operations, team, or distribution. SEA Fund focuses on SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, D2C, and B2B businesses, with a strong preference for models that demonstrate scalability and the potential to expand across the India-SEA corridor. For Indian founders, the fund offers a meaningful strategic edge beyond capital: its regional network can open doors to Southeast Asian markets at an earlier stage than most investors can facilitate. Founders building with a cross-border lens or those whose business models translate well into markets like Singapore, Indonesia, Vietnam, or the Philippines will find SEA Fund a particularly relevant partner. The fund positions itself as a hands-on early backer that understands the nuances of building in emerging market ecosystems where infrastructure gaps and consumer behavior can vary significantly from Western benchmarks.

investors.name: IIMA Ventures
investors.thesis: Nurture startups from IIM Ahmedabad ecosystem and beyond
investors.notes: IIMA's venture arm; supports alumni and student-founded startups
investors.writeup: IIMA Ventures is the venture and accelerator arm of IIM Ahmedabad, one of India's most prestigious business institutions. It was established to channel the intellectual capital, alumni network, and institutional credibility of IIMA into backing early-stage founders. While the program has a natural affinity for IIMA alumni and student ventures, it also considers high-quality startups from outside the IIM ecosystem that align with its broader mandate. IIMA Ventures operates across all sectors, making it relevant for founders working in consumer, B2B, fintech, deeptech, healthcare, or social impact, among others. The fund typically writes cheques in the $50k to $500k range, positioning it squarely for pre-seed and seed rounds where institutional validation matters as much as the capital itself. Beyond funding, IIMA Ventures offers access to a dense network of IIMA alumni who are operators, investors, and domain experts across industries. For first-time founders in particular, the combination of structured support, brand credibility, and a warm alumni network can meaningfully accelerate early growth. Founders with an IIMA connection should prioritise this as a high-conviction early backer, and those without should still consider applying if their fundamentals are strong.

investors.name: Elevation Capital
investors.thesis: Partner with exceptional founders building technology-driven businesses in India
investors.notes: Formerly SAIF Partners; backed Meesho, ShareChat, Unacademy, Urban Company
investors.writeup: Elevation Capital is one of India's most respected and consistently active venture capital firms, operating under its current brand after years of investing as SAIF Partners. The firm has a strong track record of backing category-defining consumer internet, fintech, SaaS, B2B, and AI businesses in India, with a clear orientation toward technology-driven models that have the potential to scale meaningfully in the Indian market. Elevation typically leads or co-leads rounds and writes cheques ranging from roughly one million to thirty million dollars, making it relevant for founders raising at seed, Series A, or Series B stages. The firm is known for being founder-friendly and hands-on, offering not just capital but strategic guidance, hiring support, and ecosystem connections over the long term. Portfolio companies like Meesho, ShareChat, Unacademy, and Urban Company reflect a consistent pattern of backing mission-driven founders early and supporting them through multiple rounds. Founders who are building in large, underserved Indian markets with a technology-first approach and strong unit economics ambitions will find Elevation Capital a natural conversation partner. Outreach is best done through warm introductions from existing portfolio founders or ecosystem connections.

investors.name: IvyCap Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest in IIT alumni-founded and other high-quality tech startups
investors.notes: IIT-alumni driven VC; portfolio includes LetsTransport, SalaryBox
investors.writeup: IvyCap Ventures is a technology-focused venture capital firm built around the IIT alumni ecosystem, one of the most dense and high-calibre founder networks in India. The fund invests from Seed through Series A, writing cheques typically in the range of $500K to $5M, making it relevant for startups at early inflection points who need both capital and credibility. IvyCap's differentiation lies in its alumni network, which gives portfolio founders access to operators, co-investors, and senior advisors from IITs across India and globally. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, DeepTech, and HealthTech, reflecting a broad appetite for technology-driven business models. Portfolio companies like LetsTransport and SalaryBox reflect their interest in scalable platforms solving real operational problems in the Indian market. If you are an IIT-pedigree founder, IvyCap should be a priority conversation given their structural alignment with your profile. Non-IIT founders with strong technical differentiation in their focus sectors are also encouraged to engage. The team is India-headquartered and operationally hands-on, which matters at early stages when strategic guidance is as important as the cheque itself.

investors.name: IvyCap Ventures Advisors Private Limited
investors.thesis: Invest in IIT alumni-founded and high-quality tech startups
investors.notes: Investment advisory entity of IvyCap Ventures
investors.writeup: IvyCap Ventures is an institutional venture capital firm with a differentiated focus on startups founded or co-founded by IIT alumni, alongside other high-caliber tech-driven teams. The firm operates through IvyCap Ventures Advisors Private Limited and deploys capital at Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A stages, writing cheques typically between $500k and $5M. Their sector focus spans SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, and DeepTech, reflecting a preference for businesses with strong technology foundations and defensible market positions. What sets IvyCap apart in the Indian VC landscape is its structured access to the broader IIT alumni ecosystem, which the firm actively leverages for portfolio introductions, talent, and follow-on support. For founders, this translates into more than just capital as the network can open doors to enterprise customers, senior hires, and co-investors. Founders who are IIT alumni or who have built technically rigorous products will find IvyCap a well-aligned institutional partner. The firm is India-focused and understands the nuances of building scalable technology businesses in the domestic market while targeting global ambitions.

investors.name: Sales Force Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest in enterprise cloud companies that extend the Salesforce ecosystem
investors.notes: Salesforce's corporate VC arm; global portfolio; invested in India enterprise cos
investors.writeup: Salesforce Ventures is the corporate venture arm of Salesforce, one of the world's leading enterprise software companies. It invests globally in cloud and SaaS businesses, with a clear strategic lens: portfolio companies should extend, complement, or integrate meaningfully with the Salesforce platform and ecosystem. For Indian founders, this is a significant opportunity given the maturation of India's enterprise SaaS sector and the growing global demand for India-built B2B software. Salesforce Ventures typically writes cheques in the range of $5M to $50M, making it most relevant for founders raising Series A and beyond who have demonstrated product-market fit and initial enterprise traction. Beyond capital, the firm offers access to Salesforce's vast enterprise customer base, go-to-market partnerships, and AppExchange distribution, which can meaningfully accelerate revenue for the right portfolio company. Founders building in areas such as AI-powered CRM, sales intelligence, customer success, revenue operations, or enterprise workflow automation are likely to find strong strategic alignment. Given the corporate VC structure, expect a due diligence process that evaluates both financial potential and strategic fit with Salesforce's broader product direction and customer ecosystem.

investors.name: 8i Ventures
investors.thesis: Back India's most ambitious founders with capital and community
investors.notes: India early-stage VC; strong community of operators and founders
investors.writeup: 8i Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on India, investing at Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages with cheque sizes ranging from $100k to $1M. The firm backs founders building across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, B2B, and AI verticals, with a thesis centered on identifying and supporting India's most ambitious builders from the earliest stages of company formation. What distinguishes 8i Ventures in the crowded early-stage landscape is its emphasis on community: the firm has cultivated a network of experienced operators and founders who actively engage with portfolio companies, offering hands-on guidance on product, go-to-market, and hiring. For first-time or early founders in India, this access to a peer operator community can be as valuable as the capital itself. Founders raising a pre-institutional or early institutional round with a clear India market angle, particularly in enterprise software, fintech infrastructure, or AI-native products, will find 8i Ventures a relevant conversation. The team is reachable through their website and LinkedIn, and they are known to be founder-friendly in their early engagement process.

investors.name: Eaglewings Ventures
investors.thesis: Help first-time founders take flight with capital and mentoring
investors.notes: India pre-seed micro VC
investors.writeup: Eaglewings Ventures is an India-focused micro VC that sits at the earliest end of the funding spectrum, writing cheques between $50,000 and $300,000 at pre-seed and seed stages. The firm has built its identity around backing first-time founders, recognising that early-stage entrepreneurs often need more than just money — they need a thinking partner who can help navigate product decisions, hiring, and go-to-market strategy in the critical early months. The sectors of focus include SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and D2C, reflecting the firm's comfort with both B2B and B2C business models within the Indian context. Given the micro VC structure, founders can expect a relatively lean diligence process and faster decision-making compared to larger institutional funds. The firm positions itself as founder-first, which typically means partners are accessible and willing to roll up their sleeves post-investment. For Indian founders at the idea or early traction stage who are raising their first institutional round, Eaglewings Ventures is worth approaching, particularly if the founding team is first-generation entrepreneurs looking for a capital partner who values mentorship as much as returns.

investors.name: 247VC
investors.thesis: Always-on support for founders building ambitious companies
investors.notes: India early-stage VC with round-the-clock founder support
investors.writeup: 247VC is an India-based early-stage venture capital firm that distinguishes itself through its always-on approach to founder support. The firm invests at Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages, writing cheques in the $100k to $500k range, making it a relevant first institutional capital partner for founders who have validated early traction but need both capital and strategic guidance to accelerate. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B, covering much of the high-growth opportunity landscape in the Indian startup ecosystem. What sets 247VC apart is its operational philosophy: the team positions itself as genuinely accessible to portfolio founders beyond standard board meetings or quarterly check-ins, offering support across fundraising, hiring, GTM strategy, and product decisions as founders navigate the often turbulent early stages. For Indian founders building ambitious companies who want an engaged investor rather than a passive one, 247VC presents itself as a partner willing to be in the trenches. Founders approaching them should come prepared with clear problem articulation, early signals of market fit, and a compelling view of how they intend to build a scalable business within their chosen vertical.

investors.name: Bharat Founders Fund
investors.thesis: Invest in founders building for India's next billion consumers
investors.notes: Bharat-focused micro VC backing vernacular and rural tech
investors.writeup: Bharat Founders Fund is a micro VC focused exclusively on the India opportunity beyond metro cities. The fund backs founders at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages who are building for the next billion Indian consumers, particularly those who transact in vernacular languages, have limited digital literacy, or are entering the formal economy for the first time. Their sweet spot spans Consumer, D2C, FinTech, and AgriTech, with a strong preference for businesses where distribution innovation, regional language support, or offline-to-online models create a defensible moat. Cheque sizes range from $100k to $500k, making them a relevant lead or co-investor for founders raising their first institutional round. Founders who have deep ground-level insight into Bharat user behavior, who have built for low-cost smartphones or feature-phone adjacency, or who are solving economic inclusion challenges will find strong alignment here. The fund brings not just capital but a network oriented around scaling in non-metro geographies, which is often a practical gap for early-stage Bharat-focused startups. Founders should come prepared with clear unit economics from smaller cities and evidence of genuine user pull from their target demographic.

investors.name: Good Capital
investors.thesis: Back entrepreneurs solving India's most important problems
investors.notes: India early-stage VC; portfolio includes Kuvera, Jar, Vyapar
investors.writeup: Good Capital is an early-stage venture capital firm focused exclusively on Indian startups tackling the country's most significant and large-scale problems. The firm invests across Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages, with cheque sizes ranging from $100K to $1M, making it a relevant partner for founders raising their first or second institutional round. Good Capital has developed a strong track record in consumer and fintech, with portfolio companies like Jar, Kuvera, and Vyapar demonstrating the firm's ability to identify breakout product-market fit early. The firm's sector focus spans consumer, fintech, healthtech, SaaS, and B2B, reflecting a broad appetite for both direct-to-consumer models and enterprise plays built for the Indian context. Founders approaching Good Capital should expect a thesis-driven conversation around the depth and urgency of the problem being solved, the size of the addressable opportunity in India, and the founder's unique insight or advantage. Given their early-stage orientation, Good Capital tends to engage closely with founding teams, offering hands-on support alongside capital. Startups with strong India-first narratives and early traction signals are well positioned to resonate with the team.

investors.name: Panthera Peak
investors.thesis: Invest in early-stage technology startups in India
investors.notes: Early-stage micro VC
investors.writeup: Panthera Peak is an early-stage micro VC based in India that backs technology founders at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages. The firm writes cheques ranging from $50,000 to $300,000, making it a relevant first institutional capital partner for founders who are building their initial product, finding early traction, or assembling a core team. Panthera Peak focuses on four core verticals: SaaS, Consumer, FinTech, and AI, reflecting the firm's conviction in software-driven business models and the continued digitisation of the Indian economy. As a micro VC, Panthera Peak typically moves faster than larger institutional funds and can engage meaningfully with founders at a stage when the company may not yet have significant revenue or a fully formed team. Founders approaching Panthera Peak should come prepared with a clear articulation of the problem they are solving, the technology differentiation they bring, and their go-to-market thinking for the Indian or global market. Given the early-stage mandate, the team and founder quality tend to be strong evaluation criteria alongside the market opportunity.

investors.name: peercheque
investors.thesis: Peer-to-peer driven startup investing and ecosystem building
investors.notes: Community investment platform
investors.writeup: PeerCheque is a community-driven investment syndicate that brings together peer investors to back early-stage startups at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages. Its model is built around the idea that startup investing works better when it is collaborative, transparent, and community-led, rather than gated behind traditional fund structures. For founders, this means access to a network of investors who are actively engaged in the ecosystem, not just passive capital providers. PeerCheque typically writes cheques between $50,000 and $300,000 and focuses on sectors including SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B, making it particularly well-suited for founders building scalable, technology-enabled businesses. The platform's peer-to-peer approach means that deal evaluation and support often involve multiple perspectives from operators, founders, and domain experts within the community. For Indian founders at the earliest stages who need both capital and ecosystem validation, PeerCheque offers an entry point into a collaborative investor network that can also open doors to follow-on syndication and warm introductions. Founders should expect an engaged, community-oriented process rather than a conventional institutional diligence cycle.

investors.name: Mars Shot Ventures
investors.thesis: Back bold founders taking moonshots to build transformative companies
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Mars Shot Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that invests in founders who are pursuing bold, category-defining ideas. The firm operates at the Seed and Pre-Series A stages, writing cheques between $250,000 and $2 million, making it relevant for startups that are past the idea stage and beginning to show early traction or product-market fit signals. Their sector focus spans SaaS, DeepTech, FinTech, Consumer, and AI, reflecting a broad appetite for technology-driven businesses with transformative potential. The Mars Shot ethos signals that the firm is particularly drawn to non-obvious bets and founders who are willing to tackle large, complex problems rather than playing it safe. For founders approaching Mars Shot Ventures, it helps to frame the pitch around a compelling vision of a fundamentally different future, backed by a credible founding team and a clear understanding of the market opportunity. The firm is oriented toward the Indian startup ecosystem but is likely open to India-headquartered or India-linked businesses with global ambitions. Founders at the earliest stages of their fundraising journey will find Mars Shot Ventures a relevant and accessible early institutional partner.

investors.name: OTP Ventures
investors.thesis: Partner with exceptional founders building scalable technology companies
investors.notes: India-focused VC founded by operators; Kunal Suri, Suhail Sameer
investors.writeup: OTP Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture firm led by operators-turned-investors Kunal Suri and Suhail Sameer. Suhail brings significant credibility in the Indian startup ecosystem as the former CEO of BharatPe, giving the firm a particularly sharp lens on FinTech, consumer internet, and high-growth B2B businesses. The partnership is built around the belief that the best support a VC can offer comes from having sat in the founder's seat. OTP Ventures writes cheques typically ranging from $500k to $5M across Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A rounds, making it relevant for founders at the earliest meaningful institutional stages. The firm is sector-focused on SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, B2B, and AI, which maps well to where Indian technology entrepreneurship is most active today. Founders approaching OTP Ventures can expect investors who understand the operational realities of building in India, including distribution challenges, unit economics pressure, and the nuances of scaling across a complex market. If you are building a technology-first, scalable business and want investors who have navigated the Indian startup journey themselves, OTP Ventures is worth a direct conversation.

investors.name: Prath Ventures
investors.thesis: Back founders leveraging technology to build scalable businesses in India
investors.notes: India early-stage VC founded by Harman Sachdeva
investors.writeup: Prath Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm founded by Harman Sachdeva, focused on backing technology-driven startups across India at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages. The firm typically deploys cheques ranging from $100,000 to $1 million, positioning it as a meaningful early institutional partner for founders who are past the idea stage and looking to accelerate growth with their first or second round of professional capital. Prath Ventures invests across SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, D2C, and B2B sectors, reflecting a broad but technology-forward mandate. The firm's thesis centers on founders who are building scalable businesses with strong unit economics and defensible models suited to the Indian market. For founders, Prath Ventures represents an accessible entry point into institutional funding without the dilution pressures of larger rounds, while still gaining a partner invested in the long-term trajectory of the business. Founders pitching Prath Ventures should be prepared to articulate clear technology leverage, a well-defined Indian market opportunity, and a credible path to scale. Given its early-stage focus, strong founder conviction and team quality are likely to be key evaluation criteria.

investors.name: Aeravti Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest at the earliest stage in technology-first founders
investors.notes: India pre-seed micro VC
investors.writeup: Aeravti Ventures is an India-focused micro VC operating at the pre-seed and seed stages, designed for founders who are building before the metrics that larger funds require. The firm writes cheques in the $50k to $300k range, making it one of the few institutional vehicles willing to lead or participate at the very earliest stages of company formation in the Indian startup ecosystem. Their sector focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and DeepTech, with a consistent preference for technology-first founders who are solving real problems with a defensible technical or product insight at the core. Aeravti is not a passive check writer. Founders can expect engagement on early go-to-market strategy, fundraising positioning for the next round, and access to the firm's network within the Indian and global startup ecosystem. Given the cheque size and stage, they are typically among the first institutional names on a cap table, which means founders should approach them with a clear articulation of the problem, the founding team's edge, and an early product or prototype. If you are raising a pre-seed round of under $500k in India and come from a technical background, Aeravti Ventures is a relevant conversation to have early.

investors.name: Bulleon Ventures
investors.thesis: Back ambitious founders building high-growth technology companies
investors.notes: India early-stage VC
investors.writeup: Bulleon Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the very beginning of their journeys, typically at pre-seed and seed stages. The firm writes cheques in the range of $100,000 to $500,000, making it relevant for founders raising their first institutional capital or building conviction ahead of a larger seed round. Bulleon's sectoral focus spans SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, and B2B businesses, reflecting an interest in technology-driven models with strong unit economics potential and scalable distribution. The firm's stated orientation toward ambitious founders signals an appetite for bold market theses rather than incremental ideas. For Indian founders, Bulleon represents a domestically rooted investor that understands the nuances of building in India, including market timing, distribution challenges, and the path from early traction to Series A readiness. Founders approaching Bulleon should come prepared with a clear articulation of the problem, early evidence of product-market fit or strong founder-market fit, and a compelling view of how the business scales. Given the cheque size, Bulleon is often a lead or co-lead investor at pre-seed and can be a meaningful anchor for seed rounds.

investors.name: Mount Judi Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest in founders solving India's large structural problems with technology
investors.notes: India early-stage VC backed by experienced operators
investors.writeup: Mount Judi Ventures is an India-focused early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the Seed and Pre-Series A stages. The firm is backed by experienced operators, meaning the team brings direct company-building context rather than purely financial perspectives, which can be valuable for first-time founders navigating early product, go-to-market, and hiring challenges. Mount Judi's core investment thesis centres on founders who are deploying technology to address India's large structural problems, spanning sectors such as SaaS, FinTech, Consumer, B2B, and AI. Their typical cheque size ranges from $250,000 to $2 million, making them a relevant conversation for founders raising their first meaningful institutional round. Founders approaching Mount Judi should come prepared with a clear articulation of the structural inefficiency they are solving, evidence of early traction or strong domain insight, and a credible path to scale within the Indian context. Given their operator-led DNA, the firm tends to engage substantively on execution strategy beyond just capital deployment. If your business sits at the intersection of technology and an underserved Indian market need, Mount Judi Ventures is worth a direct, thesis-aligned outreach.

investors.name: PointOne Capital
