The firm has built a distinctive identity around backing founders who are building for real India — the hundreds of millions of users coming online outside metros, often in regional languages and with very different consumption behaviors than early urban internet users. Their portfolio reflects this conviction clearly: ShareChat in vernacular social, KukuFM in regional audio, Lokal in hyperlocal news, and Vyapar in small business accounting all speak to the same underlying thesis. Cheque sizes typically range from approximately 75 lakhs to 1.5 crore, making them a practical first institutional partner for founders at the idea or early traction stage. India Quotient is particularly well-suited for founders building consumer or SMB products with a regional or mass-market angle, where deep cultural understanding and distribution insight matter more than pure technology. If your product is designed for the next wave of Indian internet users rather than existing urban tech-savvy consumers, India Quotient is a natural fit to approach early.

investors.name: ITI Growth Opportunities
investors.thesis: ITI Growth Opportunities backs early-stage Indian startups from Pre-Seed through Series A, writing focused cheques to help founders with strong fundamentals scale into market leaders across sectors.
investors.notes: BOLT, Redwing Labs, Evolve Snacks
investors.criteria: A good mix of founder credibility, product market fit and over all traction
investors.writeup: ITI Growth Opportunities is an Indian venture capital firm that invests across Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A stages with cheque sizes ranging from approximately $100,000 to $600,000. The firm takes a sector-agnostic approach, backing founders across verticals including deep tech hardware, consumer brands, and technology-driven businesses, as evidenced by portfolio companies such as BOLT, Redwing Labs, and Evolve Snacks. This breadth suggests the team evaluates investments on the strength of founding teams, market opportunity, and early traction rather than limiting itself to a single theme. For founders, ITI Growth Opportunities is most relevant at the point where capital is needed to validate product-market fit or accelerate early commercial momentum. The cheque size is well-calibrated for Indian startups at the pre-institutional stage, making it a practical lead or co-investor in rounds where runway extension meaningfully de-risks the business. Founders approaching ITI should be prepared to articulate a clear path to scalable unit economics and demonstrate early signals of demand in their target market.

investors.name: Growth valley
investors.thesis: Growth Valley is an Indian syndicate that backs early-stage to growth-stage startups across all sectors, connecting founders with a curated network of angel investors and co-investors to deploy collective capital efficiently.
investors.notes: Growth Valley operates as a syndicate model, meaning deal-by-deal participation rather than a fixed fund structure. Founders should expect a community-driven due diligence process involving multiple syndicate members before a commitment is made.
investors.writeup: Growth Valley is an India-based investment syndicate that supports startups at stages ranging from Pre-Seed through Series B and beyond. As a syndicate, it pools commitments from individual angel investors and HNIs on a deal-by-deal basis, which means founders benefit from both capital and a broader network of experienced backers rather than a single institutional check writer. The platform is sector-agnostic, making it accessible to founders building across consumer tech, SaaS, fintech, healthtech, deeptech, and other verticals. For early-stage founders, Growth Valley can be a practical bridge between friends-and-family rounds and institutional venture capital, offering validation from a group of engaged investors. The syndicate model also means that timelines can vary depending on how quickly members express interest in a given deal, so founders should factor that into their fundraising planning. Engaging with Growth Valley works best when founders come prepared with a clear use-of-funds breakdown and a compelling narrative, as the pitch needs to resonate across a diverse group of individual syndicate participants rather than a single investment committee. Their website at growthvalley.in serves as the primary point of contact for deal submissions.

investors.name: Prime Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Back visionary founders solving fundamental problems using technology
investors.notes: Backed Happay, Unacademy, Niyo, DotPe, Freo, Saasguru
investors.writeup: Prime Venture Partners is a Bengaluru-based early-stage venture capital firm that partners with founders at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages, typically deploying cheques in the range of $1 million to $3 million. The firm focuses primarily on FinTech, SaaS, HealthTech, AI, and Consumer sectors, backing founders who are tackling fundamental, large-scale problems through technology. Prime VP is widely respected in the Indian startup ecosystem for going beyond capital and offering substantive operational support to portfolio companies, particularly around product development, go-to-market strategy, and early talent acquisition. The team brings a combination of operating and investing experience that resonates well with first-time and repeat founders alike. Their portfolio includes well-known names such as Happay, Unacademy, Niyo, DotPe, Freo, and Saasguru, reflecting a consistent ability to identify breakout companies early. Founders pitching Prime VP should come prepared with a sharp articulation of the core problem they are solving, evidence of early market insight, and a credible view on why technology is the defining lever for their solution. The firm values long-term partnership and tends to stay closely involved through the early scaling journey.

investors.name: Peak Sustainability Ventures
investors.thesis: Invest in companies building sustainable solutions for India's climate and environmental challenges
investors.notes: India CleanTech-focused fund; portfolio at peakventures.in/investments
investors.writeup: Peak Sustainability Ventures is an India-focused venture capital firm dedicated exclusively to the CleanTech and sustainability space. The fund backs founders building solutions at the intersection of technology and environmental impact, with a particular focus on energy, agriculture, water, and broader climate verticals. Their investment range spans Seed through Series A, with typical cheque sizes between $2M and $5M, making them a relevant partner for startups that have validated core technology and are moving toward early commercial traction. Peak is oriented toward the specific structural challenges India faces around climate resilience, resource scarcity, and clean energy transition, meaning founders addressing these themes with a clear India-market lens are most likely to resonate. Startups that have begun generating early revenue, have a defensible technology or business model, and can articulate a pathway to meaningful environmental impact alongside commercial returns are well positioned to engage with the fund. Founders should review the existing portfolio on their website to understand sector depth before reaching out, and come prepared with both impact metrics and unit economics as Peak evaluates both dimensions seriously.

investors.name: 3one4 Capital
investors.thesis: Back founders who solve large problems for India and the world with technology and systems
investors.notes: Licious, BankOpen, Jupiter, Tracxn Labs, Darwinbox
investors.writeup: 3one4 Capital is a Bengaluru-based venture capital firm that invests at the earliest stages of a company's journey, writing cheques from Pre-Seed through Series A. The firm backs founders who are building technology-driven businesses with the potential to address large problems for Indian and global audiences. Their portfolio reflects a genuine breadth of sector exposure, spanning consumer brands like Licious, neobanking and fintech with BankOpen and Jupiter, enterprise SaaS with Darwinbox, and data intelligence with Tracxn. This diversity signals a thesis driven more by founder quality and problem scale than by narrow sector mandates. 3one4 is known within the Indian ecosystem for being actively involved with portfolio companies beyond capital, often contributing to hiring, strategy, and follow-on fundraising. Founders typically describe the team as accessible and intellectually engaged. Cheque sizes range from approximately $250,000 to $5 million, making them well-suited for pre-product-market-fit teams as well as those entering a more defined scaling phase. For early-stage Indian founders building for scale, 3one4 Capital is considered one of the more founder-aligned institutional options at the entry stage.

investors.name: The Venture Guys
investors.thesis: The Venture Guys is an India-based syndicate backing early-stage startups across all sectors at Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages, writing cheques around $1M by pooling capital from a curated network of investors.
investors.notes: Operates as a syndicate model, meaning deal-by-deal participation rather than a traditional blind-pool fund. Founders get access to a collective of angels and operators rather than a single decision-maker. Active across sectors, making it accessible to startups outside niche verticals.
investors.writeup: The Venture Guys is an Indian investment syndicate that backs early-stage founders from Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A. Unlike traditional VC funds, the syndicate model means capital is raised deal-by-deal from a network of investors, which can result in faster initial conversations but may require the lead to rally co-investors before a cheque closes. Their standard deployment size sits around $1M per deal, positioning them well for rounds where a founder needs a meaningful anchor or co-lead alongside other investors. Because they invest across all sectors, founders from consumer tech, SaaS, fintech, deeptech, or D2C are all fair game. The practical implication for founders is that a strong relationship with the syndicate lead matters enormously since that person champions your deal internally to the broader network. Prepare a tight investment memo alongside your pitch deck, as syndicate members often review materials asynchronously. Given their India focus and early-stage mandate, traction validation, founder-market fit, and a clear path to the next institutional round are likely the key diligence levers. Ideal for founders seeking not just capital but a distributed set of operator-investors who can open doors across the Indian startup ecosystem.

investors.name: Faad Network
investors.thesis: Democratize startup investing by connecting founders to a curated syndicate of 2000+ investors
investors.notes: Blu-Smart, Battery Smart, Grip, New Shop, Kerela Banana chips ,W Cube
investors.writeup: FAAD Network is one of India's active syndicate platforms designed to bridge the gap between early-stage founders and a large, organized network of angel investors. Rather than relying on a single check writer, FAAD pools capital from its community of 2000+ curated investors to deploy cheques typically ranging from $100,000 to $300,000, making it relevant for startups raising at the Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A, or Series A stage. The platform is sector-agnostic and has backed companies across diverse verticals including electric mobility, fintech infrastructure, D2C food brands, and retail tech, which indicates openness to both deep-tech and consumer-oriented businesses. For founders, the syndicate model means faster access to a broad investor base in a single close rather than running multiple parallel conversations. FAAD also offers founders visibility within its investor network, which can be valuable for follow-on fundraising and business development. Founders who are raising sub-Series A rounds and want structured syndicate participation alongside strategic networking should find FAAD a relevant platform to engage with early in their fundraise.

investors.name: Innoven Capital
investors.thesis: Provide venture debt to high-growth, VC-backed startups in India and Southeast Asia
investors.notes: Byjus , Swiggy , Infra market (200+)
investors.criteria: Problem, team , TAM , unit economics
investors.processNotes: Sector & Stage agnostic looking to partner with exciting pre-A/A companies
investors.writeup: Innoven Capital is one of India's leading venture debt firms, specializing in providing structured debt financing to VC-backed startups that are looking to extend runway or fund specific growth initiatives without further diluting founder equity. Unlike traditional equity investors, Innoven offers loan-based capital that is repaid over a defined tenure, making it particularly useful between equity rounds or as a complement to a primary equity raise. The firm is active across all major sectors and works with startups from the Seed stage all the way through Series B and beyond, with typical cheque sizes ranging from INR 10 crore to INR 100 crore depending on the company's stage and capital needs. Innoven's portfolio includes some of India's most recognized consumer and B2B names, reflecting their comfort with high-velocity, capital-intensive business models. For founders, engaging with Innoven generally requires having an existing institutional equity backer and demonstrable revenue traction, as venture debt is typically underwritten against the credibility of co-investors and the startup's growth trajectory. Their presence in Southeast Asia also makes them a strong partner for India-origin startups with regional ambitions.

investors.name: Eques Capital
investors.thesis: Eques Capital backs early-stage Indian startups from Pre-Seed through Series A across technology-driven sectors including SaaS, D2C, FinTech, and DeepTech, with a focus on founders building scalable, high-impact businesses.
investors.notes: Cusmat, Rukart, Collekto
investors.criteria: First criterion are the Product, Market, Founder fit. We then seek business model, Revenue model, market, growth & scalability, promoter integrity and vision, on-ground verification of business, potential risks and mitigation strategies, Moat and capability to disrupt the market.
investors.processNotes: We do not believe merely in board-room management rather we work shoulder to shoulder with the promoter to take the company forward. We do provide a 360 degree ecosystem to our portfolio companies and provide decisive leadership and strong expertise in business transformation which addresses the gaps in businesses, and paves way for optimal value creation by unlocking the true potential of the business.
investors.writeup: Eques Capital is an Indian venture capital firm that invests across a broad spectrum of early-stage startups, from Pre-Seed all the way through Series A. Their portfolio signals an appetite for both B2B technology plays and consumer-facing businesses, spanning enterprise SaaS, B2B marketplaces, D2C brands, FinTech, Logistics, HealthTech, CleanTech, DeepTech, PropTech, Creator Economy, and ESG-aligned ventures. The firm's cheque size flexibility, ranging from $15,000 to $2,000,000, means they can engage meaningfully with founders at very different stages of capital need, from a founder running early pilots to a startup ready for a structured Seed round. Known portfolio companies include Cusmat in enterprise learning, Rukart in B2B commerce, and Collekto in FinTech-driven debt collections, suggesting they appreciate founders solving real operational inefficiencies in underserved markets. For Indian founders, Eques Capital represents a generalist early-stage partner willing to engage across sectors and ticket sizes, making them worth approaching with a clear problem statement, early traction, and a strong view on the Indian market opportunity.

investors.name: Eximius Ventures
investors.thesis: Eximius Ventures backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed to Pre-Series A, with a focus on capital-efficient businesses across SaaS, FinTech, Web3, HealthTech, and emerging sectors like CleanTech and the Creator Economy.
investors.notes: Jar, Eka Care
investors.writeup: Eximius Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm investing in Indian startups from Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A. The firm writes cheques in the range of $100,000 to $500,000, making it a meaningful first institutional check for founders who are still finding product-market fit or preparing for a larger seed round. Eximius takes a broad sectoral view, actively backing companies in enterprise and SMB SaaS, B2B marketplaces, FinTech, Web3, HealthTech, CleanTech, Gaming, and the Creator Economy. Portfolio companies like Jar and Eka Care signal that Eximius is comfortable with both consumer and B2B models, particularly those targeting underserved Indian users or building foundational digital infrastructure. Founders approaching Eximius should expect engagement beyond just capital; the team is known to work closely with early-stage founders on go-to-market strategy, hiring, and follow-on fundraising preparation. Given the cheque size and stage focus, Eximius is well suited for founders who have a validated idea and an early team but need a credible institutional partner to anchor their pre-seed or seed round before approaching larger funds.

investors.name: Rohit Taneja
investors.thesis: Rohit Taneja backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages, with a focus on SaaS (enterprise and SMB), FinTech, and Creator Economy businesses that demonstrate strong product thinking and founder-market fit.
investors.notes: Super K, OneImpression, Tilt, GetSupp, Leap Club
investors.criteria: Team ->> Market ->> Product
investors.processNotes: Serial Founder. Passive Angel Investor. Part of the FirstCheque group for larger deals.
investors.writeup: Rohit Taneja is an individual angel investor based in India, writing Pre-Seed and Seed cheques typically in the range of $8,000 to $25,000. His investment interest spans SaaS for enterprise and SMB audiences, FinTech, and the Creator Economy, reflecting a preference for software-driven business models with scalable unit economics. His portfolio includes OneImpression, one of India's notable influencer marketing platforms, along with Super K, Tilt, GetSupp, and Leap Club — companies that span creator tools, consumer wellness, and community-first products. This breadth suggests Rohit is comfortable backing founders operating at the intersection of product and distribution innovation. For founders, Rohit is best approached when you have early traction or a compelling product hypothesis and are assembling a syndicate of angels rather than closing a single lead. Given his ticket size, he typically co-invests alongside other angels or micro-funds. Reaching out with a concise product story, clear articulation of the target customer, and evidence of early user love tends to resonate with angel investors of his profile. He likely adds value beyond capital through product feedback and network introductions within the Indian startup ecosystem.

investors.name: Ashvik Kapital
investors.thesis: Ashvik Kapital backs early-stage Indian startups across D2C, FinTech, Logistics, and Health Tech, deploying syndicated capital from Pre-Seed through Series A to founders building scalable, consumer-facing or technology-driven businesses.
investors.notes: TABP,Vinverse
investors.criteria: Management Background, Business model, addressable market, path to profitability
investors.writeup: Ashvik Kapital is an Indian syndicate investing in early-stage startups from Pre-Seed to Series A, with cheque sizes ranging from $100K to $1M. The firm focuses on four high-conviction sectors: D2C, FinTech, Logistics, and Health Tech, reflecting a preference for businesses addressing large, tangible market opportunities in India's consumption and infrastructure story. As a syndicate, Ashvik Kapital pools capital from multiple investors, which means founders benefit not just from a single lead but from a broader network of co-investors who often bring sector-specific expertise, distribution connections, and follow-on support. The team has visible associations with TABP and Vinverse, suggesting active participation in India's organised angel and early-stage investing ecosystem. This network positioning can be particularly valuable for founders at the Pre-Seed or Seed stage who need smart money alongside their first institutional or semi-institutional round. Founders pitching Ashvik Kapital should come prepared with a clear unit economics narrative, a defined India-market go-to-market strategy, and evidence of early traction or strong founder-market fit, as syndicate investors typically move quickly when the story is crisp and the round structure is clean.

investors.name: International Finance Corporation (IFC)
investors.thesis: IFC backs high-growth emerging market businesses across all sectors, focusing on companies with strong development impact — job creation, financial inclusion, and sustainability — typically at Series A and beyond with meaningful equity cheques.
investors.notes: upGrad, BigBasket, Lenskart, Moglix, LeadSquared
investors.writeup: International Finance Corporation is the private sector investment arm of the World Bank Group and one of the most active development finance institutions deploying capital into high-growth emerging markets, including India. IFC typically invests at Series A and beyond, writing cheques in the range of five to fifty million dollars, and looks for businesses that combine commercial scale with measurable development impact — whether through job creation, expanding access to essential services, climate solutions, or financial inclusion. In India, IFC has backed category leaders across edtech, e-commerce, eyewear, B2B commerce, and SaaS, including upGrad, BigBasket, Lenskart, Moglix, and LeadSquared, signalling openness to a broad range of sectors. Beyond capital, IFC brings significant value through its global institutional network, policy relationships, and ESG frameworks that can help founders build governance credibility with future co-investors and public market stakeholders. For Indian founders, an IFC investment often carries a strong signal of institutional quality. Founders raising Series A or later rounds with a clear social or economic impact angle — particularly in climate, healthcare, agriculture, or financial services — should actively consider approaching IFC as a strategic institutional partner.

investors.name: DHOLAKIA VENTURES
investors.thesis: Dholakia Ventures backs early-stage Indian startups across all sectors, writing early cheques at Pre-Seed through Series A to help founders build durable, high-impact businesses.
investors.notes: Dhiwise, Zypp Electric, StockGro, White.inc, and many more.
investors.writeup: Dholakia Ventures is an Indian family office that actively deploys capital at the earliest and most formative stages of a startup's journey, from Pre-Seed through Series A. With a cheque size starting around INR 10 Lakh, the firm positions itself as a conviction-driven, founder-friendly backer that enters before most institutional investors are willing to take the risk. This makes Dholakia Ventures particularly relevant for founders who are still validating their product or assembling their core team and need a credible name on their cap table to catalyze further funding. The portfolio reflects a genuinely sector-agnostic approach, with investments spanning SaaS tooling for developers through Dhiwise, clean mobility through Zypp Electric, retail investing through StockGro, and consumer brands through White.inc. Founders can expect a family office dynamic, meaning decisions tend to be faster and less committee-driven than a traditional VC fund, with the principals directly engaged. For Indian founders at the zero-to-one stage who want patient, relationship-oriented capital alongside strategic introductions within the Indian startup ecosystem, Dholakia Ventures is a strong early conversation to pursue.

investors.name: The Endless Network
investors.thesis: The Endless Network backs high-conviction founders across all sectors from Pre-Seed through Series A, co-investing through a curated syndicate model to deploy meaningful capital into scalable Indian startups.
investors.notes: upGrad, BigBasket, Lenskart, Moglix, LeadSquared
investors.writeup: The Endless Network is an Indian investment syndicate that writes cheques of approximately $300,000 across Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A rounds. It does not restrict itself to a single sector, making it relevant for founders across consumer internet, SaaS, B2B commerce, and beyond. The syndicate model means capital is pooled from a curated network of operators, angels, and professionals, which often brings strategic value beyond just funding. Portfolio companies such as upGrad, BigBasket, Lenskart, Moglix, and LeadSquared indicate a track record of backing businesses that have gone on to achieve significant scale, suggesting the network has access to quality deal flow and has been active across multiple market cycles. For early-stage founders, the syndicate structure can be advantageous because it brings together multiple investors in a single close, reducing the time spent managing individual conversations. Founders should approach The Endless Network with a clear articulation of their market size, early traction metrics, and a compelling team story, as syndicates typically move faster when conviction is high among lead members of the network.

investors.name: Dexter Angels
investors.thesis: Dexter Angels is an early-stage syndicate backing pre-seed and seed startups across all sectors in India, writing focused cheques to help founders get their first institutional conviction.
investors.notes: Fello, Glamyo, Neuropixel, Pilgrim
investors.writeup: Dexter Angels is an Indian angel syndicate that invests at the pre-seed and seed stages across all sectors, making it a relevant early conversation for founders who are raising their first or second round. The syndicate model means Dexter Angels pools capital from a network of individual angels for each investment, which can bring both cheque size and a distributed network of mentors and operators alongside the funding. Their cheque range of roughly 75,000 to 200,000 USD is sized appropriately for rounds where founders need lead or co-lead support without diluting heavily. The portfolio spans consumer internet, fintech, healthtech, deep tech, and D2C, with names like Fello, Glamyo, Neuropixel, and Pilgrim signalling comfort with both tech-first and brand-led businesses. Founders should approach Dexter Angels with a clear problem statement, early traction or strong founding team credentials, and openness to working with a syndicate structure rather than a single institutional check writer. Given their broad mandate, differentiated market positioning and founder-market fit tend to be the strongest entry points for a productive first conversation.

investors.name: Originity (Origin To Eternity LLP)
investors.thesis: Originity backs early-stage startups at Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A in Health Tech, CleanTech, and Education, writing focused cheques of $20,000–$50,000 to founders building purposeful, impact-oriented businesses.
investors.notes: https://angel.co/sachinoswal
investors.criteria: Passion (Team), Mission (Idea), Execution
investors.processNotes: I invest my time, money & energy behind startups that I love.
investors.writeup: Originity, operating under the LLP Origin To Eternity, is a family office investing at the earliest stages of a startup's journey — Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A. With a typical cheque size ranging from $20,000 to $50,000, Originity is suited for founders who are raising their first institutional or near-institutional round and need a committed, values-aligned backer rather than a large institutional fund. The investment focus spans three sectors with significant India relevance: Health Tech, CleanTech, and Education. These are areas where technology-driven solutions can create meaningful impact at scale across Tier 1 and Tier 2 India. The family office structure means founders can expect a more direct and personal relationship with the principal, faster decision-making cycles, and a patient capital outlook compared to a traditional VC fund with LP pressure. The AngelList presence indicates openness to engaging with founders through digital platforms and syndicated rounds. Founders approaching Originity should come with a clear problem statement, early traction or validation in their target sector, and an articulate view on how their work drives long-term impact alongside commercial returns.

investors.name: Inno-Vest Advisors
investors.thesis: Inno-Vest Advisors backs early to growth stage startups across sectors, writing INR 1–3 Cr cheques through its syndicate and advisory model to connect founders with curated networks of investors.
investors.notes: Inno-Vest operates as a syndicate and advisory platform, likely pooling angel and HNI capital for deals across Seed through Series B+ rounds. Their sector-agnostic stance makes them accessible to founders across verticals. Founders engaging with them should expect a facilitated deal process rather than a single GP-led fund structure.
investors.criteria: FDD
investors.writeup: Inno-Vest Advisors is a syndicate and advisory firm active across early and growth stage startup investing in India. Operating with a sector-agnostic mandate, the platform writes cheques in the INR 1 to 3 Cr range and participates across Seed, Pre-Series A, Series A, and Series B and beyond rounds. Rather than functioning as a traditional venture fund, Inno-Vest acts as a deal facilitation and advisory platform, likely aggregating capital from angel investors, HNIs, and family offices into structured syndicate rounds. This model can be particularly valuable for founders looking to close rounds efficiently while accessing a broader investor network beyond a single check writer. For early stage founders, this means Inno-Vest can help fill round allocations with relatively modest ticket sizes while also providing advisory support around fundraising strategy. Founders reaching out should be prepared to articulate a clear capital deployment plan and growth narrative, as syndicate platforms typically require concise, investor-ready materials to circulate across their network. Given their all-sectors approach, differentiated business models and strong founding teams are likely key evaluation criteria.

investors.name: Namay Kedia
investors.thesis: Namay Kedia backs early-stage Indian startups across all sectors at Pre-Seed to Pre-Series A stages, deploying syndicate capital to help founders navigate the critical zero-to-one phase.
investors.notes: Namay Kedia operates as a syndicate, meaning deal-by-deal co-investment is likely pooled from a network of angels rather than a single fund. Founders should expect a collaborative diligence process and potential value-add from syndicate members beyond the lead cheque.
investors.writeup: Namay Kedia is an Indian angel syndicate that writes cheques ranging from approximately $15,000 to $150,000 into startups at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages. Operating as a syndicate rather than a traditional venture fund, the platform aggregates capital from a curated group of angels and operators for each deal, which can bring diverse domain expertise and networks alongside the investment. The sector-agnostic approach means founders across consumer tech, B2B SaaS, fintech, healthtech, and other verticals can explore fit. For Indian founders, syndicates like this are particularly relevant at the early stage where institutional funds may not yet be active, and the ticket size sits well in the gap between friends-and-family rounds and larger institutional Seed rounds. Founders approaching Namay Kedia should be prepared with a clear problem statement, early traction or strong founder-market fit narrative, and an articulate use-of-funds plan for the raise. Given the syndicate model, responsiveness and clarity in materials such as a crisp deck and financial model will be especially important to facilitate broader co-investor buy-in within the network.

investors.name: Magnivia Ventures
investors.companyTypeRaw: Venture Capital Firm, Syndicate, Broker Dealer and Consulting
investors.thesis: Magnivia Ventures backs early-stage startups across SaaS, FinTech, SpaceTech, and DeepTech, writing cheques from $150K to $1.5M and supporting founders from Seed through Series B and beyond via its syndicate and consulting capabilities.
investors.notes: tathya.earth and helloclever.co
investors.criteria: Burn Rate, ARR, market size, past investors, founder experience and founder EQ and IQ
investors.processNotes: We are currently raising our fund and any current investment are made through our syndicate.
investors.writeup: Magnivia Ventures is a multi-modal investment platform that combines a venture capital fund, syndicate network, broker-dealer function, and consulting practice under one roof. This structure allows the firm to engage with startups at Seed, Pre-Series A, Series A, and later stages, deploying cheques typically between $150K and $1.5M while also facilitating larger rounds through syndication. The firm's sector focus spans enterprise and SMB SaaS, FinTech, SpaceTech, and DeepTech, reflecting an appetite for both capital-efficient software businesses and more technically complex, long-horizon bets. For Indian founders, Magnivia's broker-dealer capability can be particularly useful when navigating cross-border fundraising or structured investment arrangements. The consulting layer means the team is likely to engage substantively on business model and go-to-market questions rather than functioning purely as a capital provider. Portfolio companies like tathya.earth and helloclever.co suggest the firm is comfortable backing founders working at the intersection of frontier technology and real-world applications. Founders in B2B SaaS, fintech infrastructure, or deep-tech verticals with global ambitions would be well-suited to explore a conversation with Magnivia.

investors.name: 77 Capital
investors.thesis: 77 Capital backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages, focusing on SaaS, B2B marketplaces, FinTech, and HealthTech through a syndicate model that brings together aligned capital and operator networks.
investors.notes: Mewt, Fego, Clinikally, Vidyut Tech, M2P, Hyperface
investors.criteria: Tend to turnaround quickly, primarily calls with the founders + 3rd party due diligence (if required)
investors.processNotes: Primarily Focussed on Fintech as 77 Capital + focus on other sectors in individual capacity
investors.writeup: 77 Capital is an Indian investment syndicate that writes cheques of USD 75,000 to 100,000 into Pre-Seed and Seed stage startups. Its portfolio reflects a clear conviction around B2B software and infrastructure businesses, with investments spanning enterprise and SMB SaaS, B2B marketplaces, fintech, and health tech. Companies like M2P and Hyperface signal comfort with fintech infrastructure and API-led business models, while Clinikally and Fego point to interest in digital health and consumer wellness built on strong tech foundations. Vidyut Tech and Mewt further demonstrate a pattern of backing asset-light, scalable Indian startups solving real enterprise or platform problems. As a syndicate, 77 Capital offers founders more than just capital; the model typically means co-investors and domain-relevant angels come in alongside the lead, which can be valuable for startups seeking both money and market access. Founders pitching to 77 Capital should be prepared to articulate clear unit economics, a defensible B2B go-to-market strategy, and a path to scalable revenue. The typical entry point is early enough to help shape the company, making a crisp product narrative and a strong founding team the most important factors in the conversation.

investors.name: Rise Capital
investors.thesis: Invest in the best technology companies in emerging markets across India, LATAM, Middle East, Africa and Southeast Asia
investors.notes: Mojocare, Stockgro, TradeX, SaveIn to name a few
investors.criteria: The 5-M framework
investors.processNotes: A Tiger Global spin-off and a Silicon Valley-based VC fund focused on emerging markets across the globe - LATAM: Brazil, Mexico; Middle East; Africa: Nigeria, Egypt; Asia: India & SEA. Headquartered in San Francisco and launched in 2014 by long-time Emerging Market internet entrepreneur and investor, Nazar Yasin (ex-Tiger Global and Goldman Sachs, and former CEO of Forticom - acquired by LSE: MAIL), Rise Capital’s partnership consists of experienced internet executives and entrepreneurs who possess 100+ years of combined operating and investing experience in Emerging Markets, including “unicorn” (US$1bn+) exits in every major region of the world.
investors.writeup: Rise Capital is a global venture capital firm with a strong focus on emerging markets, with India being a core geography alongside LATAM, the Middle East, Africa, and Southeast Asia. The firm invests across the full startup lifecycle, from Seed and Pre-Series A all the way through Series B and later rounds, giving founders the potential for a long-term capital partnership rather than a one-time check. Rise Capital covers an exceptionally broad sector mandate, including SaaS, FinTech, D2C, eCommerce, Gaming, Web3, HealthTech, CleanTech, DeepTech, SpaceTech, Logistics, PropTech, Creator Economy, and more, which means sector-specific founders across verticals can find relevance here. Their Indian portfolio includes consumer and fintech plays like StockGro, SaveIn, and TradeX, reflecting an appetite for both B2C and B2B models with strong growth dynamics. With cheque sizes ranging from $100K to $100M, Rise Capital can meaningfully engage with a first-time founder raising a seed round or a scaled company looking for a larger growth investment. Founders with cross-border ambitions across emerging markets may find particular resonance given Rise Capital's truly global lens.

investors.name: Titan Capital
investors.thesis: Back exceptional founders building iconic consumer and technology brands in India
investors.notes: Ola, Dealshare, Mamaearth, OfBusiness, Razorpay, Snapdeal, Urban Company
investors.writeup: Titan Capital is one of India's most founder-respected early-stage venture funds, run by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal — the co-founders of Snapdeal who bring operator-level empathy to their investing. The fund focuses on pre-seed, seed, and pre-Series A rounds, typically deploying cheques in the $100,000 to $500,000 range. Their portfolio spans consumer brands, fintech, B2B commerce, and internet businesses, reflecting a broad sectoral appetite rather than a narrow vertical thesis. What sets Titan Capital apart for founders is the combination of hands-on mentorship from operators who have built at scale in India and a network that opens doors across hiring, co-investors, and enterprise partnerships. The team is known to move relatively quickly and engage substantively with founders at the idea and early traction stage. If you are building something ambitious in consumer or technology in India and are at the zero-to-one phase, Titan Capital is worth a warm introduction. Founders who resonate with their portfolio ethos — high conviction, execution-first, India-native problems — are likely to find a receptive audience here.

investors.name: Smilodon Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Smilodon Venture Partners backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages across sectors, writing small but conviction-driven cheques to help founders get their first institutional capital and build foundational momentum.
investors.notes: BankSaathi, Zypp Electric
investors.criteria: Founders profile, Idea, Unit economics, Market potential, Financials
investors.writeup: Smilodon Venture Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on Pre-Seed and Seed investments in Indian startups. With a cheque size ranging from $10,000 to $50,000, the firm is positioned to participate in rounds where founders are raising their very first external capital, making it particularly relevant for bootstrapped founders looking to close their first institutional ticket. The firm takes a generalist stance, investing across sectors rather than restricting itself to a single vertical. Portfolio companies like BankSaathi, operating in fintech distribution, and Zypp Electric, building EV-powered last-mile delivery infrastructure, reflect an appetite for startups solving real operational and financial inclusion challenges in India. For founders, Smilodon can be a practical early backer to anchor a Pre-Seed round or fill out a Seed syndicate where larger cheques from bigger funds are leading. Given the lean cheque size, founders should approach Smilodon with a clear use-of-funds narrative and evidence of early traction or a compelling problem statement. Fit is strongest for founders who are capital-efficient and can demonstrate meaningful milestones on relatively modest funding.

investors.name: Fuise.in (Connecting Startups and VCs in A Minute)
investors.thesis: Fuise.in operates as a fundraising matching platform connecting Indian startups with investors across all stages and sectors, aiming to make the fundraising discovery process faster and more efficient for both founders and capital allocators.
investors.notes: Fuise.in is a tech-enabled matchmaking platform designed for the Indian startup ecosystem, bridging the gap between early-stage and growth-stage startups and a curated network of VCs, angels, and family offices. Founders can expect structured introductions rather than a traditional investment relationship. Useful for founders who want to expand their investor outreach beyond warm networks.
investors.processNotes: Fuise is fundraising matching platform that helps the founders to connect with multiple investors to connect in more faster way through single registration. Our founders expects 10-11 average calls monthly from investors.
investors.writeup: Fuise.in is an Indian fundraising matching platform built to reduce friction in the startup-investor discovery process. Rather than functioning as a direct investor, Fuise.in acts as an intermediary that connects founders with relevant investors across Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A, Series A, and Series B and beyond stages, covering all sectors of the Indian startup ecosystem. The platform positions itself around speed and relevance, promising connections in a short turnaround time compared to traditional outreach methods. For founders struggling to identify the right investor fit or lacking warm introductions into VC networks, Fuise.in offers a structured channel to surface their fundraising opportunity to a broader set of capital allocators. The cheque size range it caters to, from ten thousand dollars up to twenty million dollars, suggests it serves startups at nearly every early to growth stage. Founders should approach Fuise.in as a pipeline-building tool rather than a direct funding source. It is particularly relevant for founders outside major metro networks or those doing their first institutional round who need efficient access to India's investor community without relying solely on personal networks.

investors.name: Brigade REAP
investors.thesis: Brigade REAP backs early-stage PropTech startups at the seed stage, focusing on innovations that can transform the real estate, construction, and built-environment ecosystem in India.
investors.notes: Snaptrude
investors.criteria: VC investible businesses, Team, Product, Market, GTM, Technology
investors.writeup: Brigade REAP is the PropTech-focused investment and accelerator arm of Brigade Group, a leading real estate developer headquartered in Bangalore with a significant presence across South India. Operating as a syndicate at the seed stage, Brigade REAP deploys cheques around $70,000 into startups building at the intersection of technology and the built environment. What makes Brigade REAP particularly compelling for PropTech founders is the combination of capital and strategic proximity to an active real estate developer, offering potential for pilots, enterprise access, and real-world validation within Brigade Group's own projects and partner network. The syndicate is well-suited for founders working on construction technology, design tools, smart buildings, facilities management, or any technology that can be applied within the development, sales, or operations lifecycle of real estate. Snaptrude, a well-regarded collaborative BIM and design platform, is a known portfolio company, reflecting Brigade REAP's appetite for deep-tech solutions targeting architects, developers, and construction professionals. Founders approaching Brigade REAP should be prepared to articulate a clear deployment pathway within the Indian real estate market and ideally demonstrate early traction or a credible pilot opportunity.

investors.name: GetFunded
investors.thesis: Connect founders with the right investors through curated matchmaking
investors.notes: India fundraising platform with angel/VC network
investors.criteria: 1. Issue or suffering being addressed 2. Method, perhaps capturing economic value 3. Tech prowess, scaling, and GTM. 4. Founder: Background, narrative, market fit, etc.
investors.writeup: GetFunded is an India-based fundraising platform designed to simplify the capital-raising journey for early-stage startups. It operates at the intersection of technology and investor relations, offering founders structured access to a curated network of angel investors and venture capital firms across the country. The platform supports startups raising across Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A rounds, with cheque sizes typically ranging from $100,000 to $1 million, making it particularly relevant for founders in the early innings of institutional fundraising. GetFunded's core value proposition lies in its matchmaking infrastructure, which aims to reduce the friction and time typically associated with building an investor pipeline from scratch. Rather than relying on warm introductions alone, founders can leverage the platform to surface relevant investors based on sector fit, stage, and geography. For Indian founders who may lack established networks in the startup ecosystem, GetFunded serves as a meaningful entry point to credible capital conversations. The platform is sector-agnostic, making it broadly applicable across consumer tech, SaaS, fintech, healthtech, and other verticals popular in the Indian startup landscape.

investors.name: O2 Angel Network LLP
investors.thesis: O2 Angel Network backs early-stage Indian startups across all sectors, writing syndicated cheques from pre-seed through Series B, with a preference for technology-driven and deep-tech ventures solving real-world problems.
investors.notes: Skye, Eeki Foods, Green Tiger, BosonQ PSI, Navars, Tutti Frutti, Amaara Herbs, Fabheads, Cultyvate, ZiffyTech, Urban Matrix, Brainwired,
investors.criteria: Standard Process
investors.writeup: O2 Angel Network LLP is an India-based angel syndicate that deploys capital across the full early-stage spectrum, from pre-seed ideation through Series B growth rounds. Operating as a syndicate, the network aggregates commitments from multiple angels to write meaningful cheques in the USD 100K to USD 500K range, giving founders a structured and credible investor on their cap table rather than a fragmented collection of individual angels. The portfolio reflects genuine sector diversity, spanning deep-tech and simulation software through BosonQ PSI, advanced materials manufacturing through Fabheads, food and agri-tech through Eeki Foods and Cultyvate, consumer wellness through Amaara Herbs and Tutti Frutti, healthtech through ZiffyTech, and urban mobility through Urban Matrix. This breadth signals that O2 evaluates founders and market opportunity over rigid sectoral mandates. For early-stage founders in India who need both capital and network leverage, O2 Angel Network offers the combined conviction of a coordinated angel group with the flexibility typical of early-stage syndicate investing. Founders pitching here should be prepared to articulate a clear problem statement, a defensible solution, and a scalable India or global market opportunity.

investors.name: Beej Network
investors.thesis: Beej Network backs early-stage Indian startups from Pre-Seed through Pre-Series A across all sectors, writing structured angel cheques to support founders at the ground level before institutional capital arrives.
investors.notes: Swytchd, Crib, Vested, Microfinance.ai
investors.criteria: On basis of the team and the business model
investors.writeup: Beej Network is an Indian angel network that focuses on early-stage startups at the Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A stages, making it a relevant first institutional cheque for founders who are still finding product-market fit or preparing for a larger raise. With a standard cheque size of around $100K, Beej is positioned to provide meaningful early capital without the complexity of a full venture fund process. Their portfolio spans fintech platforms like Vested and Microfinance.ai, proptech through Crib, and emerging consumer tech with Swytchd, reflecting a genuinely sector-agnostic approach rather than a narrowly themed mandate. For founders, this means the network evaluates team quality, market opportunity, and execution potential rather than fitting you into a predefined vertical. Being an angel network, Beej can also bring individual domain expertise and warm introductions from its member base alongside capital, which is particularly useful for founders navigating early customer or partner conversations. Founders raising a first or bridge round in India and seeking a collaborative, founder-friendly syndicate structure should consider reaching out to Beej Network directly through their website.

investors.name: BLinC Invest
investors.thesis: BLinC Invest backs early-stage Indian startups at the Pre-Series A stage, with a focus on FinTech and EdTech ventures that leverage technology to expand financial access or transform learning outcomes.
investors.notes: Fingg, Get Vital
investors.writeup: BLinC Invest is an Indian venture capital firm that concentrates on Pre-Series A opportunities in FinTech and EdTech, two sectors where India's scale and digital infrastructure create outsized growth potential. The firm targets startups that have moved past the ideation stage and can demonstrate early product-market fit, user traction, or revenue signals. With a typical cheque size of $1 million to $3 million, BLinC is well-positioned to lead or co-lead Pre-Series A rounds, giving founders meaningful capital to build teams, refine their go-to-market strategy, and prepare for a Series A raise. Known portfolio bets include Fingg and Get Vital, suggesting the firm is comfortable backing founders solving problems at the intersection of financial services, consumer behaviour, and technology-enabled access. Founders approaching BLinC should come prepared with a clear articulation of their unit economics, distribution strategy, and the regulatory landscape relevant to their sector. The firm operates within the Indian startup ecosystem and is likely to add value through sector-specific networks in financial services and education. Founders in adjacent spaces such as InsurTech, WealthTech, or learning platforms may also find alignment with BLinC's broader investment lens.

investors.name: AltInvest1
investors.thesis: AltInvest1 backs early-stage Indian startups across all sectors from Pre-Seed through Series A, writing cheques of USD 100K to USD 500K via an online investment platform that connects founders with a curated network of investors.
investors.notes: Eeki Foods, ZiffyTech, YellowPlate, Nexstem
investors.writeup: AltInvest1 is an online investment platform that facilitates early-stage funding for Indian startups, operating across Pre-Seed, Seed, Pre-Series A, and Series A stages. The platform is sector-agnostic, making it a viable destination for founders building across verticals including agri-tech, health-tech, food-tech, and deep-tech. Cheque sizes range from USD 100K to USD 500K, positioning AltInvest1 well for founders seeking meaningful early capital without the complexity of a large institutional round. Its portfolio signals genuine diversity in business models and problem statements, suggesting the investment team evaluates founders and market opportunity on merit rather than adhering to a narrow thematic focus. For founders, AltInvest1 is worth approaching if you are raising your first institutional round or a bridge ahead of a larger Series A, and can demonstrate early traction or a compelling product insight. The online platform model also implies a relatively structured and accessible deal-flow process, which can be an advantage for first-time founders navigating the Indian fundraising landscape for the first time.

investors.name: Multiply Ventures
investors.thesis: Back founders building consumer-first businesses in India
investors.notes: India consumer-focused early stage VC; founded by Raveen Sastry
investors.writeup: Multiply Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on the Indian consumer market, founded by Raveen Sastry. The firm invests at the Pre-Seed and Seed stages, writing cheques between $100,000 and $500,000, making it well-suited for founders raising their first institutional round or a structured seed round. The core thesis centers on backing consumer-first businesses across D2C, eCommerce, FinTech, Health Tech, and Consumer Internet sectors. Multiply Ventures takes a conviction-driven, founder-centric approach, with the general partner bringing meaningful operator perspective to the table, which translates into practical support beyond capital. For Indian founders building brands, platforms, or products aimed at the domestic consumer, Multiply Ventures is a relevant early conversation to have. Given its stage focus, the firm is best approached when founders have early proof points around product-market fit or strong founder-market conviction. Outreach through LinkedIn or warm introductions from the broader Indian startup ecosystem is advisable. Founders should be prepared to articulate their understanding of the Indian consumer and a clear path to building a differentiated, scalable business.

investors.name: Cloud Capital
investors.thesis: Cloud Capital backs early-stage Indian startups across a wide range of sectors, writing syndicate-style cheques at Pre-Seed through Series A with a preference for SaaS, FinTech, DeepTech, and emerging technology categories.
investors.notes: Airmeet, Rupifi, Orange Health, OneCode, FrontRow, Jar, Lysto, etc
investors.writeup: Cloud Capital is an Indian syndicate that participates in early-stage funding rounds from Pre-Seed all the way through Series A. The syndicate writes cheques in the range of $100,000 to $150,000, making it a meaningful early backer for founders looking to complement larger institutional rounds or fill out a round with experienced syndicate capital. The portfolio reflects a genuinely broad sectoral appetite, spanning enterprise and SMB SaaS, FinTech, B2B marketplaces, HealthTech, DeepTech, DevTools, Gaming, CleanTech, SpaceTech, Web3, and the Creator Economy. Past bets include well-known Indian startups such as Airmeet, Rupifi, Orange Health, OneCode, FrontRow, Jar, and Lysto, signaling comfort with both consumer and B2B models at an early stage. For founders, Cloud Capital is worth approaching if you are raising a Pre-Seed or Seed round and want syndicate participation from investors familiar with the Indian startup ecosystem. Given the breadth of the portfolio, founders across most technology verticals have a credible reason to reach out, and the syndicate structure can move relatively quickly once conviction is established.

investors.name: Long Tail Ventures
investors.thesis: Long Tail Ventures backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed to Pre-Series A with small but conviction-led cheques, focusing on capital-efficient businesses across SaaS, B2B marketplaces, D2C, FinTech, and emerging sectors like Web3, CleanTech, and DeepTech.
investors.notes: Clinikally, ZFW Dark Stores, STAGE, Elixir Protocol, etc.
investors.criteria: Team, Founder-Market fit
investors.processNotes: As operators from India & the US----- we move quick (2 calls max) & can bring in our global network of founders, funds, & CXOs.
investors.writeup: Long Tail Ventures is an early-stage venture capital firm writing cheques between USD 35,000 and USD 100,000 across Pre-Seed, Seed, and Pre-Series A rounds in India. The firm takes a broad sectoral stance, backing founders in SaaS for enterprise and SMB, B2B marketplaces, eCommerce and D2C brands, FinTech, Logistics, Health Tech, Consumer Internet, Web3, CleanTech, DeepTech, and DevTools. The portfolio reflects genuine range: Clinikally in D2C health and skincare, ZFW Dark Stores in quick commerce infrastructure, STAGE in regional language streaming, and Elixir Protocol in the Web3 space. For founders, the relatively small cheque size means Long Tail Ventures is often accessible at the very first institutional moment, making it a practical first call for pre-revenue or early-revenue teams building in India. Given the breadth of sectors covered, founders should lead with product differentiation and a clear path to scalable unit economics. The firm appears comfortable with unconventional or niche market theses, consistent with its name and the idea that meaningful outcomes can emerge from underexplored corners of the market.

investors.name: Rajsha chemicals Pvt Ltd
investors.thesis: Rajsha Chemicals Pvt Ltd operates as a family office backing early to growth-stage Indian startups across all sectors, with a focus on founders building scalable, impact-aware businesses in areas such as sustainable mobility, climate tech, and consumer food innovation.
investors.notes: Blusmart mobility, Uravu labs, Sudo foods
investors.criteria: Multiple factors like team, market size, innovation, etc
investors.writeup: Rajsha Chemicals Pvt Ltd is a family office backed by the promoters of a chemicals business, deploying patient, proprietary capital into Indian startups from Seed through Series B and beyond. With cheque sizes ranging from $100,000 to $1,000,000, it is well suited for founders raising their first institutional or bridge rounds and looking for a long-term, low-bureaucracy capital partner. The portfolio, which includes BluSmart Mobility, Uravu Labs, and Sudo Foods, reveals a clear appreciation for startups that combine commercial ambition with meaningful impact, particularly in climate technology, sustainable infrastructure, and the future of food and consumption. As a family office, Rajsha Chemicals can move with greater flexibility and speed than institutional funds, making it especially attractive for founders who need decisive decision-making without lengthy investment committee cycles. Founders approaching this office should be prepared to articulate a credible path to scale within the Indian market while demonstrating why their business creates durable value. The cross-sector openness means founders from fintech, agritech, healthtech, or consumer sectors are equally welcome, provided the underlying business has strong fundamentals and a founder team with domain conviction.

investors.name: Singhvi Heritage LLP / JITO Angel Network
investors.thesis: Singhvi Heritage LLP, operating through the JITO Angel Network, backs early-stage Indian startups across sectors at the pre-seed to pre-Series A stage, with a preference for founders building scalable, technology-driven businesses with strong unit economics.
investors.notes: BluSmart, VideoVerse, ChargeGrid, Rooter
investors.writeup: Singhvi Heritage LLP participates in early-stage startup investing through the JITO Angel Network, one of India's more active community-anchored angel platforms. The JITO Angel Network draws on a wide base of high-net-worth individuals and family offices from the Jain entrepreneurial community, giving founders access not just to capital but to a dense network of business operators, traders, and industrialists with pan-India reach. The portfolio signals a clear appetite for technology-enabled businesses across diverse verticals — from electric mobility and EV charging infrastructure with BluSmart and ChargeGrid, to media-tech and sports gaming through VideoVerse and Rooter. This breadth suggests the investor is sector-agnostic at the early stage, prioritising founder quality and market potential over vertical specialisation. Cheque sizes in the $20,000 to $50,000 range make this a relevant partner for pre-seed and seed rounds, either as a lead or alongside other angels. Founders who can demonstrate a connection to the JITO community or present at JITO-affiliated pitch forums may find warm introductions easier to secure. The family office backing also suggests patient, relationship-oriented capital rather than purely return-driven institutional pressure.

investors.name: Skumar
investors.thesis: Backs early-stage Indian founders at pre-seed with focused conviction across frontier technology categories including FinTech, SpaceTech, Web3, DeepTech, DevTools, and Consumer Internet, writing small but meaningful first cheques to help founders get to their next milestone.
investors.notes: Skumar is an individual angel investor operating at the pre-seed stage in India. Writes cheques in the $25,000–$35,000 range, making them a suitable first institutional-style angel for founders looking to close a small round before approaching larger seed funds.
investors.writeup: Skumar is an individual angel investor who backs Indian founders at the pre-seed stage across a broad but considered set of technology verticals: FinTech, SpaceTech, Web3, Consumer Internet, DeepTech, and DevTools. The cheque size of $25,000 to $35,000 positions Skumar as a meaningful early backer who can help a founding team bridge the gap between a working prototype or early traction and a formal seed round. For founders, this profile signals someone comfortable with high-uncertainty, high-ambition bets at the very earliest stage, which is relatively rare in the Indian ecosystem where most capital enters at seed or later. Founders in deep technology or infrastructure categories like SpaceTech or DevTools will find the appetite here particularly relevant, as these sectors often struggle to attract angel capital in India at such an early stage. If you are building in one of the listed verticals, have a compelling founding team, and are looking to close a small but credible pre-seed round, Skumar is worth a direct and concise outreach. Keep your pitch focused on the problem, why now, and why your team is the right one to build this.

investors.name: Ecosystem Ventures
investors.thesis: Ecosystem Ventures backs early-stage Indian startups at the Pre-Series A stage across sectors, writing cheques in the $3–$30 million range to support founders building scalable businesses with strong fundamentals.
investors.notes: Ecosystem Ventures operates as a sector-agnostic VC firm focused on the Pre-Series A gap in the Indian startup ecosystem. Their relatively wide cheque size range suggests flexibility to lead or co-invest depending on deal context. Founders should be prepared to discuss unit economics and a clear path to Series A readiness.
investors.writeup: Ecosystem Ventures is an India-focused venture capital firm that targets the Pre-Series A stage, a critical and often underserved inflection point in a startup's journey. With a cheque size range of $3 million to $30 million, the firm has the capacity to lead rounds or take meaningful co-investment positions, making them a relevant partner for founders who have moved past the seed stage but are not yet ready for a full Series A institutional raise. Being sector-agnostic, Ecosystem Ventures evaluates opportunities across consumer, B2B, fintech, SaaS, and other verticals, which means founders do not need to fit a narrow thematic mandate to get a meeting. For founders approaching them, the conversation will likely centre around proof of early traction, clarity on how the capital will be deployed to reach Series A milestones, and the quality of the founding team. Given their positioning in the ecosystem, they are likely attuned to the challenges of scaling in India's diverse and price-sensitive markets. Founders should arrive with a clear narrative on why now is the right time to scale and what defensibility looks like in their category.

investors.name: Sprout Venture Partners
investors.thesis: Sprout Venture Partners backs early-stage Indian startups at Pre-Seed and Seed stages across sectors, writing cheques of around Rs 40–42 lakh (approximately $500K) to help founders validate and scale their core business model.
investors.notes: Pixis, Ripplr, Advantage Club, Fashor, Advarisk, Rusk Media
investors.criteria: Focus on PMF
investors.writeup: Sprout Venture Partners is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on Pre-Seed and Seed investments in Indian startups. The firm takes a sector-agnostic stance, having backed companies across AI-driven marketing technology, B2B distribution, employee engagement, fashion D2C, risk analytics, and the creator economy. This breadth signals that Sprout evaluates founders and market opportunity rather than restricting itself to a narrow vertical. With a cheque size of around $500,000, it is well suited for founders raising their first institutional round or a bridge into a larger Seed. The portfolio names suggest comfort with both technology-first and operationally intensive business models, which is a useful signal for founders across the startup spectrum. Founders approaching Sprout should be ready to articulate a clear problem statement, early traction or validation metrics, and a compelling view on why their market is large and defensible in the Indian context. Given the early stage focus, the team and founder-market fit are likely weighted heavily in evaluation. Engagement through their LinkedIn or website is a reasonable first step, and warm introductions through portfolio founders or ecosystem intermediaries will typically improve response rates.

investors.name: Blume Ventures
investors.thesis: First institutional cheque for tech-led founders solving Indian problems with global scale potential; 8–10 year partnership, ~2:1 reserve ratio.
investors.notes: Founded 2010 by Karthik Reddy & Sanjay Nath (Mumbai). AUM >$600M; Fund IV ~$290M (largest). 330+ cos: Unacademy, Slice, Spinny, Purplle, smallcase, Servify, Locus, Classplus, Pixxel, Battery Smart, Namma Yatri. Publishes Indus Valley Annual Report.
investors.criteria: Please see https://blume.vc/for-startups/
investors.processNotes: I typically respond to all mails (other than mass mails) sent to me. But it may take 2-4 days to get a reply depending on if I am travelling. But you will get a reply!
investors.writeup: Blume Ventures is India's largest homegrown early-stage venture firm, founded in 2010 by Karthik Reddy and Sanjay Nath and headquartered in Mumbai. It manages over $600 million in assets and is typically the first institutional cheque in its companies, partnering for 8–10 years. Blume has scaled deliberately across four funds: Fund I (2011–14, ₹100 Cr) wrote $200–300K pre-seed cheques; Fund II (2015–17, $60M) moved to $400–750K seed; Fund III (2018–20, $102M) ranged $750K–2.3M; and Fund IV (2021, ~$290M, its largest) writes core cheques of roughly $1–2 million, entering at seed to Pre-Series A. The firm has built one of India's strongest portfolios — unicorns and breakouts including Unacademy, Slice, Spinny, Purplle, smallcase, Servify, Locus, Classplus, LambdaTest, Pixxel, Battery Smart and Namma Yatri. Blume is known for being genuinely founder-first and for institutional thought leadership through its widely-read Indus Valley Annual Report. Its 60-member team across India and the US provides active support in talent, finance, legal and follow-on fundraising, and it maintains a roughly 2:1 reserve ratio to back winners through later rounds. For first-time and repeat founders alike, Blume is among the most trusted seed-stage partners in India.

investors.name: Caspian Equity
investors.thesis: Caspian Equity backs early-stage Indian startups at Seed and Pre-Series A across FinTech, Health Tech, CleanTech, and Food & Agritech, with a focus on capital-efficient businesses solving real problems for underserved markets.
investors.notes: Caspian Equity operates under Caspian Advisors Private Limited and writes cheques typically in the range of USD 250K to USD 1M. Their sector focus aligns with impact-adjacent themes popular among institutional and family office LPs in India.
investors.criteria: Founder - product fit, competitive advantage & potential market size
investors.processNotes: Caspian invests equity and debt capital in socially responsible, multiple bottom line businesses delivering financial and social value.
investors.writeup: Caspian Equity is a Seed and Pre-Series A focused venture capital firm investing in Indian startups across FinTech, Health Tech, CleanTech, and Food & Agritech. Their cheque sizes range from approximately USD 250,000 to USD 1,000,000, making them well-suited for founders raising their first institutional round or a bridge before a larger Series A. The firm appears to favor sectors with structural tailwinds in India, particularly businesses addressing financial inclusion, preventive healthcare access, sustainable energy transitions, and agricultural value chains. Founders approaching Caspian Equity should come prepared with a clear articulation of unit economics, a credible go-to-market strategy for India's diverse and often price-sensitive consumer base, and a founding team with relevant domain depth. Given their sector concentration, startups that demonstrate both commercial viability and a measurable positive outcome for underserved communities are likely to resonate well with their investment lens. Warm introductions through the broader Indian VC ecosystem are advisable, as is engaging with their LinkedIn presence to understand recent portfolio activity and team composition before reaching out directly.

investors.name: Beyond Next Ventures
investors.thesis: Beyond Next Ventures backs science and technology-driven startups at Pre-Seed through Series A, with a focus on DeepTech, HealthTech, AgriTech, CleanTech, and SpaceTech founders building high-impact, defensible businesses in India.
investors.notes: MediBuddy, BigHaat, Gig India, Medfin, Gromo, MUSE Diagnostics, ImpactGuru, Myelin Foundry, Faunatech, Lil Goodness, Biomoneta, Generic Aadhaar
investors.criteria: We're interested in deep-tech startups solving important social and environmental challenges. We're also keen to assess startups powering digital transformation of industries.
investors.writeup: Beyond Next Ventures operates a dedicated India investment platform as an extension of its Japan-headquartered venture practice, giving it a distinctive cross-border angle that few India-focused early-stage VCs can match. The firm writes cheques ranging from approximately $200,000 to $2,500,000, covering Pre-Seed through Series A, which means it can lead or participate at the earliest formation stages and follow on as companies gain traction. The sectoral focus spans DeepTech, HealthTech, AgriTech, CleanTech, SpaceTech, and Enterprise SaaS, with a clear preference for startups where science, proprietary technology, or hard IP forms the core of the business. Founders in regulated or capital-intensive domains such as diagnostics, biotech, precision agriculture, or space applications will find the team genuinely conversant with the technical and commercial nuances of these markets. Beyond Next Ventures also brings value beyond capital through its Japan network, which is particularly relevant for startups exploring manufacturing partnerships, regulatory approvals, or enterprise sales in the Japanese market. The portfolio signals an appetite for both B2B and B2C models as long as the technology differentiation is meaningful and the societal impact is visible.

investors.name: Vertex Ventures
investors.thesis: Vertex Ventures backs technology-driven companies across Southeast Asia and India from seed through growth stages, partnering with founders building scalable businesses with regional or global ambitions.
investors.notes: Vertex Ventures is a global VC network with a dedicated Southeast Asia and India fund that is active across early and growth stages. The firm has strong ties to the Temasek ecosystem, giving portfolio companies access to a broad network across Asia. Indian founders should note that Vertex typically looks for companies with regional expansion potential beyond just the domestic market.
investors.writeup: Vertex Ventures is a multi-stage venture capital firm operating as part of a global network with a dedicated Southeast Asia and India fund. The firm invests across a wide range of sectors and stages, from seed through Series B and beyond, making it relevant for founders at multiple points in their journey. Vertex is backed by Temasek, Singapore's sovereign wealth fund, which gives the firm deep institutional credibility and a broad network across corporate and government stakeholders in Asia. For Indian founders, Vertex is a particularly strong partner if you are building a business with ambitions beyond India, as the firm has significant on-the-ground presence and portfolio companies across Southeast Asia. The team brings operational and strategic value alongside capital, and founders can benefit from warm introductions across the regional network. Vertex tends to back technology-enabled businesses where scalability and market leadership are clear near-term goals. If you are raising a seed or early-stage round and have a regional or global thesis embedded in your model, Vertex is worth a direct outreach. Engage via LinkedIn or their official India or Singapore office contacts for the best response.

investors.name: Mayfield India
investors.thesis: Mayfield India backs early-stage technology-driven startups across sectors, partnering with founders from seed through Series A to build scalable, high-impact businesses in the Indian market.
investors.notes: Mayfield is a globally established VC with a dedicated India practice, known for backing founders at the earliest stages with patient, hands-on support. The India team operates with significant autonomy and has a strong network across enterprise tech, consumer, and deep tech. Founders typically get access to Mayfield's global platform and cross-border expertise.
investors.writeup: Mayfield India is the Indian arm of the globally respected Mayfield Fund, one of Silicon Valley's most established venture capital firms with decades of experience backing technology companies worldwide. The India practice focuses on early-stage investments spanning seed, pre-Series A, and Series A rounds, with cheque sizes typically ranging from half a million to five million dollars. The firm positions itself as a genuine early-stage partner, willing to engage with founders at the idea or MVP stage and support them through their initial scaling journey. Mayfield India does not restrict itself to a single sector, making it approachable for founders across enterprise software, consumer tech, fintech, healthtech, and emerging deep tech verticals. What distinguishes Mayfield for Indian founders is the access to a global network and institutional credibility that can help with international expansion, follow-on fundraising, and recruiting senior talent. The team is known for being founder-friendly and operationally engaged, often taking board seats and providing strategic guidance beyond just capital. For Indian startups looking for a well-networked, globally connected early-stage backer with long-term conviction, Mayfield India is a strong fit to explore.

investors.name: IndiaBiz
investors.thesis: IndiaBiz operates as an M&A and investment platform connecting early-stage Indian startups and SMEs with buyers, investors, and acquirers, focusing on Pre-Seed to Pre-Series A opportunities across all sectors.
investors.notes: IndiaBiz for Sale is one of India's established online marketplaces for business buying, selling, and fundraising. It caters to a wide range of deal sizes, making it accessible to micro-entrepreneurs, SMEs, and early-stage startups seeking capital or strategic exits.
investors.processNotes: Direct connects with Private Investors
investors.writeup: IndiaBiz, operating through its platform IndiaBizForSale, serves as a marketplace-driven investment and M&A platform in India. It is designed to bridge the gap between early-stage founders and a broad network of investors, acquirers, and strategic partners. The platform accommodates a wide cheque size range, from as low as ten thousand rupees to three million dollars, making it relevant for founders at very nascent stages all the way through to Pre-Series A rounds. Unlike traditional venture funds, IndiaBiz functions as a deal-discovery and facilitation platform, giving startups visibility to a large pool of interested investors and buyers across all sectors. For founders, this means the platform can serve both as a fundraising channel and as an early M&A exploration tool. IndiaBiz is particularly useful for founders in tier-two and tier-three cities or those building capital-efficient businesses who may not have direct access to institutional investors. Founders should prepare a crisp business summary, clear financials, and a defined ask before listing, as the platform attracts a diverse audience ranging from angel investors and family offices to strategic acquirers actively seeking opportunities in the Indian market.

investors.name: SenseAI
investors.thesis: SenseAI backs pre-seed and seed stage founders building in enterprise SaaS, SMB software, health tech, deep tech, and developer tools, writing early cheques where technical depth and product ambition intersect.
investors.notes: Skit.ai, Cureskin, Flow works, burncal, tripeur, Nexstem etc
investors.criteria: ai-first/IP, data moat, strong us gtm is enterprise/mid-market saas, solid tech founder, >$500mn SAM
investors.writeup: SenseAI is an early-stage venture capital firm focused on pre-seed and seed investments in India, with a clear preference for startups operating at the intersection of technology and real-world application. The firm writes cheques in the range of five lakh rupees and concentrates on sectors including enterprise SaaS, SMB software, health tech, deep tech, and developer tooling. SenseAI's portfolio signals a strong appetite for founders who are building technically non-trivial products — whether that is conversational AI infrastructure as seen with Skit.ai, AI-powered consumer health through Cureskin, or neurotechnology via Nexstem. The firm appears comfortable backing both B2B-first businesses and those targeting the consumer health space, suggesting flexibility in go-to-market approach as long as the underlying technology is defensible.
